definition_zh: 结构；构造；体系；构建
definition_en: the way parts are arranged and joined, an organized system, or to arrange something in a planned way
core_image: 一座建筑的梁柱彼此咬合，撑起整体形状
scene: 这座桥的结构非常坚固。 The structure of the bridge is very solid.
sceneCN: 这里 structure 是「结构」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这座桥的结构非常坚固。

结构上
重组

senses.title: How parts are joined
senses.definition: the way the parts of something are arranged and joined
senses.definitionCN: 事物各部分排列与连接的方式
senses.example: The structure of the bridge is very solid.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥的结构非常坚固。
senses.why: This is the shape held by parts.
senses.whyCN: 这是各部分撑起来的形状。

senses.title: An organized system
senses.definition: a system of parts that work together, as in society
senses.definitionCN: 各部分协同运作的体系，如社会
senses.example: The village has a simple social structure.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村子有简单的社会结构。
senses.why: Buildings and societies are both built.
senses.whyCN: 建筑与社会都是「搭」起来的。

senses.title: Arrange on purpose
senses.definition: to arrange something in a planned way
senses.definitionCN: 有计划地安排某事物
senses.example: She structured the report around three questions.
senses.exampleCN: 她围绕三个问题来组织这份报告。
senses.why: The noun becomes the act of building it.
senses.whyCN: 名词在这里变成了搭建的动作。

intro.en: Structure comes from Latin structura, a fitting together.
intro.cn: structure 来自拉丁语 structura，意为拼合、建造。

items.en: Structura meant building or arrangement.
items.cn: structura 意为建造或排列。

items.en: Struere meant to pile up or build.
items.cn: struere 意为堆起或建造。

items.en: Structure named a building's frame.
items.cn: 中古英语 structure 指建筑的骨架。

items.en: It described the parts of a whole.
items.cn: 它开始描述整体的各部分。

items.en: It also became a verb meaning to arrange.
items.cn: 它也变成动词，表示安排组织。

note.en: Structure is compared with look-alike words and with words for frameworks.
note.cn: 把 structure 与形近词以及表示框架的词作比较。

entries.definition: to fight hard

entries.definition: a supporting frame

entries.definition: the shape of something
entries.definitionCN: 形式；形状

entries.definition: a set of connected parts

normalIntro.en: Structure is the order that holds parts together.
normalIntro.cn: structure 是把各部分拢在一起的那份秩序。

normal.en: The structure of the cell is simple.
normal.cn: 这个细胞的结构很简单。

normal.en: Social structure shapes daily life.
normal.cn: 社会结构塑造着日常生活。

normal.en: Check the sentence structure again.
normal.cn: 再检查一下句子结构。

normal.en: They restructured the company.
normal.cn: 他们重组了公司。

normal.en: She structured her speech clearly.

abstract.en: Structure is a promise that parts will meet.
abstract.cn: 结构，是各部分终会相遇的承诺。

abstract.en: Remove one beam and the whole shape changes.
abstract.cn: 抽掉一根梁，整个形状就变了。

abstract.en: We build structures, and structures build us.
abstract.cn: 我们建造结构，结构也塑造我们。

examples.en: She structured the report around three questions.

sensesIntro.en: Structure is how parts fit, a system of parts, or the act of arranging them.
sensesIntro.cn: structure 是各部分如何拼合、由部分组成的体系，或把部分安排好的动作。

core.en: Beams meeting at a firm joint.
core.cn: 梁木在牢固的接点相遇。

branches.en: A bridge holds its shape.

branches.en: A village arranges its roles.

branches.en: A writer orders three points.
branches.cn: 作者排出三个要点。

branches.en: A frame of wood and a frame of roles both hold.
branches.cn: 木头的框架与角色的框架，都能撑住。

branches.en: To structure is to choose an order.

definition_zh: 减少；削减；降低；还原；（数学）约简；（烹饪）收汁
definition_en: the act of making something smaller or simpler, or the amount by which it is made smaller
core_image: 一块厚布被两边慢慢拉紧，最后缩成一小片
scene: 家里换了新锅炉之后，暖气费账单明显薄了一截。 The new boiler led to a twenty percent reduction in fuel use.
sceneCN: 这里 reduction 指「用量下降的幅度」（第 1 个义项：数量或程度变小）；句意：新锅炉使燃料用量减少了百分之二十。图中可辨识物件：旧锅炉、新锅炉、下降箭头、用量表。

pos.zh: 减少；削减；降低；（化学）还原；（数学）约简；（烹饪）收汁

collocations.zh: 归谬法（reductio ad absurdum 的英语说法）

senses.title: A decrease in amount
senses.titleCN: 数量减少：总量或程度变小
senses.definition: the act or result of making an amount, rate or level smaller
senses.definitionCN: 使数量、比率或水平变小的动作或结果
senses.example: The new boiler led to a twenty percent reduction in fuel use.
senses.exampleCN: 新锅炉使燃料用量减少了百分之二十。
senses.why: Reduction comes from Latin reducere 'to lead back'; the modern 'make smaller' sense grew from leading something down to a lower level.
senses.whyCN: reduction 出自拉丁 reducere「带回」；现代「使变小」义由「把某物带到更低水平」发展而来。

senses.title: A price cut
senses.definition: a lowering of price, often offered as a discount
senses.definitionCN: 价格的调低，常作为折扣给出
senses.example: The store advertised a fifty-dollar reduction on the jacket.
senses.exampleCN: 商店宣传这件夹克降价五十美元。
senses.why: Commerce applies the physical image of lowering to money: the price is brought down, and the amount is called a reduction.
senses.whyCN: 商业把「降低」的物理意象用于金钱：价格被带下来，降下的数额就叫 reduction。

senses.title: Chemical reduction
senses.titleCN: 化学还原：物质得到电子
senses.definition: in chemistry, the process in which a substance gains electrons and its oxidation state falls
senses.definitionCN: 化学中物质获得电子、氧化态降低的过程
senses.example: Iron ore is turned into metal by chemical reduction in a furnace.
senses.exampleCN: 铁矿石在炉中经化学还原变成金属。
senses.why: Chemists kept the 'lowering' idea: the oxidation number is brought down as electrons are added, so the reaction is a reduction.
senses.whyCN: 化学家保留了「降低」的观念：加入电子后氧化数被带低，因此该反应称为还原。

senses.title: Mathematical simplification
senses.titleCN: 数学约简：把式子化到更简形式
senses.definition: in mathematics, the rewriting of an expression or problem into a simpler equivalent form
senses.definitionCN: 数学中把表达式或问题改写为更简单的等价形式
senses.example: Reduction of the fraction 18/24 gives 3/4.
senses.exampleCN: 把分数 18/24 约简得到 3/4。
senses.why: The 'lead back' sense survives here: a complex expression is led back to its simplest equivalent.
senses.whyCN: 「带回」义在此留存：复杂表达式被带回其最简单的等价形式。

senses.title: Cooking down a sauce
senses.titleCN: 烹煮收汁：水分蒸发使汤汁变浓
senses.definition: in cooking, the evaporation of liquid so that a sauce becomes thicker and more concentrated
senses.definitionCN: 烹饪中液体蒸发、使酱汁变稠变浓的过程
senses.example: A slow reduction concentrates the flavour of the stock.
senses.exampleCN: 慢火收汁使高汤的味道更浓缩。
senses.why: The kitchen borrows the volume sense literally: the liquid is reduced in quantity while the flavour remains.
senses.whyCN: 厨房直接借用了体积义：液体数量变少，而风味保留。

senses.title: Lowering in rank
senses.titleCN: 降级：职位或地位被调低
senses.definition: the act of moving someone to a lower rank, position or status
senses.definitionCN: 把某人调到更低职级、职位或地位的行为
senses.example: His reduction from captain to private was announced at roll call.
senses.exampleCN: 点名列队时宣布他从上尉降为列兵。
senses.why: This sense is the oldest direction of ducere: a person is led back down the hierarchy.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项最贴近 ducere 的原始方向：人被沿着等级序列带回下方。

senses.title: Data reduction
senses.titleCN: 数据简化：把原始数据压缩成可用摘要
senses.definition: the process of summarizing or simplifying large sets of raw data into usable measures
senses.definitionCN: 把大量原始数据汇总或简化为可用指标的过程
senses.example: Data reduction turned thousands of sensor readings into one daily average.
senses.exampleCN: 数据简化把数千条传感器读数变成一个日均值。
senses.why: The word is applied to information rather than matter: detail is brought down to a manageable summary.
senses.whyCN: 该词被用于信息而非物质：细节被压到可处理的摘要层级。

senses.title: Reductio ad absurdum
senses.titleCN: 归谬：把命题推到荒谬以反驳它
senses.definition: in logic, the method of disproving a claim by showing that its consequences are absurd
senses.definitionCN: 逻辑中通过显示某主张的推论荒谬来反驳它的方法
senses.example: The proof proceeds by reduction to absurdity.
senses.exampleCN: 该证明通过归谬法推进。
senses.why: The Latin phrase reductio ad absurdum means 'a leading back to the absurd': the argument leads the claim back to a contradiction.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁短语 reductio ad absurdum 意为「带回到荒谬」：论证把该主张带回矛盾之处。

intro.en: Reduction comes from Latin reductio, the noun of action from reducere 'to lead back'. The English word first meant a bringing back, and later narrowed toward 'making smaller'.
intro.cn: reduction 出自拉丁 reductio，即 reducere「带回」的动作名词。英语词最初意为「带回」，后来收窄为「使变小」。

items.en: Latin ducere meant 'to lead, draw, conduct'. Its family includes conduct, produce, induce, introduce and reduce.
items.cn: 拉丁 ducere 意为「引导、拉、带领」，其词族包括 conduct、produce、induce、introduce、reduce。

items.en: Reducere joined re- 'back' to ducere, meaning 'to lead back, bring back'. It could be used for troops, for a price, or for a written argument.
items.cn: reducere 把 re-「回」加到 ducere，意为「带回、领回」，可用于军队、价格或书面论证。

items.en: The Latin action noun reductio named the act of leading back. In logic, reductio ad absurdum named a proof that leads a claim back to contradiction.
items.cn: 拉丁动作名词 reductio 指「带回」的行为。逻辑中的 reductio ad absurdum 指把主张带回到矛盾的证明。

items.en: English reduction entered in the sixteenth century, first as a bringing back or restoration, then as a lowering or diminishing.
items.cn: 英语 reduction 于 16 世纪进入，最初指带回或恢复，后指降低或减少。

items.en: Chemistry, mathematics, cooking and data processing each fixed a specialized sense of the lowering or simplifying action.
items.cn: 化学、数学、烹饪与数据处理各自固定了「降低」或「简化」动作的专门义项。

items.en: The exact first English citation is uncertain, and the deeper origin of Latin ducere is generally discussed only as a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根）：英语最早书证确切年代存疑；拉丁 ducere 的更深来源通常只能作为重构来讨论。

note.en: The first group separates the reduce family from near-looking forms; the second gives near-synonyms that stress amount, cut or simplification.
note.cn: 第一组区分 reduce 词族与形近形式；第二组给出强调数量、削减或简化的近义词。

entries.definition: To make smaller or simpler; reduction is the act or the resulting amount.
entries.definitionCN: 指使变小或变简单；reduction 是动作或由此得到的量。

entries.definition: Describing something that simplifies, often with disapproval. It is not the noun for a cut.
entries.definitionCN: 形容简化的，常带贬义；不是表示「削减量」的名词。

entries.definition: The theory that complex things can be explained by simpler parts. It is not a decrease in quantity.
entries.definitionCN: 指复杂事物可由更简单部分解释的理论，并非数量减少。

entries.definition: Logical inference from general to specific, from Latin deducere 'lead away'. The prefix changes the direction.
entries.definitionCN: 指从一般到具体的逻辑推理，出自拉丁 deducere「带走」；前缀改变了方向。

entries.definition: A general fall in amount. Reduction often implies a deliberate act by someone.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指数量下降；reduction 常暗示有人有意采取行动。

entries.definition: An often sudden or politically decided lowering, especially of budgets or staff. It is more informal than reduction.
entries.definitionCN: 常指突然或政治上决定的削减，尤指预算或人员，比 reduction 更口语。

entries.definition: A gradual worsening or falling off. It usually happens over time rather than by a single act.
entries.definitionCN: 指逐渐恶化或下降，通常随时间发生，而非由单一行动造成。

entries.definition: The act of making something easier to understand. It stresses clarity, not size.
entries.definitionCN: 指使某物更易理解，强调清晰而非规模。

entries.definition: A specific lowering of price. It overlaps sense 2 but names the commercial offer, not the general act.
entries.definitionCN: 特指价格下调，与第 2 个义项重叠，但命名的是商业优惠而非一般行为。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: re- 'back' + ducere 'lead' + -tion: leading something back down.
normal.cn: re-「回」+ ducere「引导」+ -tion：把某物带回低处。

normal.en: The family runs reduce, reductive, reducer, reductionism, irreducible.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 reduce、reductive、reducer、reductionism、irreducible。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: cost reduction, emission reduction, data reduction, reduction to absurdity.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：成本削减、减排、数据简化、归谬法。

normal.en: Chemistry says reduction when electrons are gained and the oxidation number falls.
normal.cn: 化学中，得到电子、氧化数下降就叫还原。

normal.en: deduction leads away; reduction leads back. The prefix decides the direction.
normal.cn: deduction 带走，reduction 带回；前缀决定方向。

abstract.en: Picture a thick cloth pulled tight from both sides until it shrinks to a small patch.
abstract.cn: 想象一块厚布被两边拉紧，最后缩成一小片。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of papers whittled down to a single summary card.
abstract.cn: 想象一摞文件被削成一张摘要卡。

abstract.en: Picture a sauce simmering until the surface drops and the colour deepens.
abstract.cn: 想象酱汁慢煮到液面下降、颜色加深。

examples.en: The policy aims at a thirty percent reduction in plastic waste by 2030.
examples.cn: 该政策目标是到 2030 年将塑料废物减少三成。

examples.en: Reduction of the oxide with carbon yields iron and carbon dioxide.
examples.cn: 用碳还原氧化物会生成铁和二氧化碳。

examples.en: After data reduction, the team kept only the four most stable variables.
examples.cn: 经过数据简化，团队只保留四个最稳定的变量。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（回）+ duct（引导）」——把数量往回带 → reduction 减少、削减

root: 拉丁 ducere「引导」→ reducere「带回、领回」→ reductio「带回」；英语 reduction。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all lower something: an amount, a price, an oxidation state, an expression, a sauce, a rank, a data set, or a claim driven back into contradiction.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在「把某物带低」：数量、价格、氧化态、表达式、酱汁、职级、数据集，或被带回矛盾的命题。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thick cloth drawn tight until it shrinks to a patch.
core.cn: 核心意象：厚布被拉紧，缩成一小片。

branches.en: AMOUNT AND PRICE: something is brought down, whether a quantity or a tag.
branches.cn: 数量与价格：被带低的东西，或是一个量，或是一个标价。

branches.en: CHEMISTRY: electrons are added and the oxidation number falls.
branches.cn: 化学：加入电子，氧化数下降。

branches.en: SIMPLIFICATION: expressions and raw data are led back to manageable forms.
branches.cn: 简化：表达式与原始数据被带回可处理的形式。

branches.en: KITCHEN: liquid volume falls while flavour concentrates.
branches.cn: 厨房：液体体积下降，风味浓缩。

branches.en: RANK AND LOGIC: a person is led down the hierarchy, or a claim is led back to absurdity.
branches.cn: 职级与逻辑：人沿等级被带下，或主张被带回到荒谬。

intro.en: Reduction is a Latin action noun in -tio laid onto the verb reducere, which joins 'back' to 'lead'. English keeps both the physical and the figurative directions.
intro.cn: reduction 是加在动词 reducere 上的拉丁 -tio 动作名词，该动词把「回」与「引导」结合。英语同时保留其物理与比喻方向。

latinIntro.en: The ducere family is large: conduct, produce, induce, introduce, deduce, reduce, educate and seduce all contain the 'lead' root, but each prefix sets a different direction.
latinIntro.cn: ducere 词族庞大：conduct、produce、induce、introduce、deduce、reduce、educate、seduce 都含「引导」词根，但各前缀设定不同方向。

items.example: The reduction in hours improved safety.
items.exampleCN: 工时减少改善了安全状况。

items.meaning: to bring down or make smaller
items.example: The factory reduced water use by half.
items.exampleCN: 工厂把用水量减少了一半。

items.example: The review called the argument reductive.
items.exampleCN: 评论称该论证过于化约。

items.meaning: a device or substance that lowers something
items.meaningCN: 使某物降低的装置或物质
items.example: A pressure reducer sits before the valve.
items.exampleCN: 阀门前装有一个减压器。

items.meaning: cannot be made simpler or smaller
items.meaningCN: 不能进一步简化或缩小的
items.example: The problem is irreducible to one cause.
items.exampleCN: 这个问题无法化约为单一原因。

items.example: The deduction follows from the two premises.
items.exampleCN: 该推论由两个前提推出。

items.meaning: to lead into; to bring about
items.example: Warmth induces the seeds to sprout.

definition_zh: 民意调查；投票；选举；得票数；做民意调查；获得（票数）
definition_en: a survey of people's opinions, the act or result of voting, and the verbs for surveying people or receiving a number of votes
core_image: 一只手拿笔，把人群按人头一一点过，每点一个画一道
scene: 大选前一周，街角的志愿者拿着写字板，拦住过往行人问他们会投给谁。 The newspaper's latest poll shows the two candidates almost level.
sceneCN: 这里是「民意调查」（第 1 个义项：按抽样询问一批人的意见）；句意为该报最新的民调显示两名候选人几乎不相上下。画面里有街角、写字板和停下来的行人。

pos.zh: 民意调查；投票；选举；得票数
对……做民意调查；获得（票数）

derivatives.zh: 由 poll 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -ster 构成，义为「民调机构人员；民意调查员」
由 poll 加 -ing 构成，义为「投票；民意调查」
由 poll（头顶）加 -ed 构成，用于牛羊，义为「无角的」

senses.title: A survey of people's opinions
senses.definition: a survey that asks a sample of people what they think about an issue, a product or a candidate
senses.definitionCN: 就某个议题、产品或候选人询问一批抽样对象看法的调查
senses.example: An opinion poll suggested that most voters wanted the plan changed.
senses.exampleCN: 一项民意调查显示，多数选民希望这个方案作出修改。
senses.why: The word first meant a head, then a count of heads; asking people one by one repeats that counting gesture, so a survey inherits the image of ticking off person after person.
senses.whyCN: 这个词先指「头」，再指「按人头点数」；挨个询问正是重复那个点数的动作，于是民调继承了「一个个人画勾」的画面。

senses.title: The act of voting
senses.definition: the occasion on which people cast votes, usually in the phrase the polls or go to the polls
senses.definitionCN: 人们投下选票的场合，常见于 the polls 或 go to the polls 这样的说法
senses.example: The country went to the polls in the middle of a heat wave.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家在一场热浪中举行了投票。
senses.why: Once a poll is a head count, the day when heads are counted becomes the poll itself, and voters are said to go to it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 poll 是「清点人头」，清点人头的那一天本身就成了 poll，选民也就被说成「走向」它。

senses.title: The number of votes recorded
senses.definition: the total of votes won by a candidate or party, or the record of those totals
senses.definitionCN: 某位候选人或政党赢得的票数总和，或记录这些数字的清单
senses.example: The final poll gave the mayor a clear majority.
senses.exampleCN: 最终得票数让市长获得了明显的多数。
senses.why: If the count produces a number, the same noun can name that number, which is how a poll comes to mean the tally a candidate watches all night.
senses.whyCN: 既然清点会得出一个数字，同一个名词就能指那个数字，于是 poll 也指候选人整夜盯着的计票结果。

senses.title: To ask people for their opinions
senses.definition: to question a group of people in order to find out what they think
senses.definitionCN: 为了解一批人的想法而向他们提问
senses.example: She polled her students about which book to read next.
senses.exampleCN: 她就下一本读什么书征求了学生们的意见。
senses.why: The noun names the survey, so the verb names the work of producing one: someone has to go out and put the questions.
senses.whyCN: 名词指调查本身，动词就指做出这项调查的过程：总得有人走出去把问题问出来。

senses.title: To receive a particular number of votes
senses.definition: to win or record a stated number or share of votes in an election
senses.definitionCN: 在选举中获得或记录下某一数字或比例的选票
senses.example: The party polled forty percent of the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 该党获得了四成选票。
senses.why: Because a poll is also the tally, the verb can be used from the other side: a candidate polls the votes that the count gives him.
senses.whyCN: 既然 poll 也指计票结果，动词就能从另一头来用：候选人 poll 到的，就是清点之后记在他名下的票。

intro.en: Poll is a Germanic word for the head that entered English from Dutch; the political senses grew out of counting people head by head, not out of Latin.
intro.cn: poll 是来自荷兰语、意为「头」的日耳曼词；它的政治义项是从「按人头点数」长出来的，与拉丁语无关。

items.en: Middle Dutch pol meant the head or the top of something, and it is generally traced to a Germanic stock rather than to Latin.
items.cn: 中古荷兰语 pol 意为头或某物的顶部，一般认为它上溯到日耳曼语来源，而不是拉丁语。

items.en: Middle English polle named the head, and by extension a person counted as one head in a crowd.
items.cn: 中古英语 polle 指头，引申为人群中被当作「一个头」来数的人。

items.en: A poll became a count of heads, then the record of votes at an election, and finally the place where those votes were cast.
items.cn: poll 由「清点人头」变成选举中的计票，再变成投票的场所。

items.en: Newspapers and social research gave the word its survey sense: a sample of heads asked for their opinions.
items.cn: 报纸与社会研究赋予这个词「调查」义：抽出一批人头来问他们的看法。

items.en: Modern English keeps the noun for a survey, a vote and a tally, and uses the verb both for asking people and for the votes a candidate wins.
items.cn: 现代英语保留名词的「调查、投票、计票」三义，动词则既指去问人，也指候选人赢得的票数。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on this Germanic head word, with one spelling twin from a different root; the near-meaning group gathers words for surveys and voting.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在这个日耳曼「头」词上的形式，并附一个来自别的词根的拼写近邻；近义组收表示「调查」与「投票」的词。

entries.definition: A person who conducts opinion polls.
entries.definitionCN: 从事民意调查的人。

entries.definition: The act of voting, or of asking people for their views.
entries.definitionCN: 投票的行为，或向人征询意见的行为。

entries.definition: Of cattle: hornless, from the old sense of the top of the head.
entries.definitionCN: 指牛羊无角的，来自「头顶」这一旧义。

entries.definition: A long thin post; it is only spelling-alike, since it comes from a Latin word for a stake, not from the word for a head.
entries.definitionCN: 长杆；只是拼写相近，词源不同，它来自拉丁语中表示「木桩」的词，与「头」这个词无关。

entries.definition: A study that collects answers from a group of people.
entries.definitionCN: 向一群人收集答案的研究。

entries.definition: The system or paper by which people vote.
entries.definitionCN: 投票的制度或选票本身。

entries.definition: A formal choice made in an election.
entries.definitionCN: 选举中作出的正式选择。

entries.definition: To go round an area asking for votes or opinions.
entries.definitionCN: 在某一地区走访拉票或征求意见。

normalIntro.en: The whole family grows from one concrete act: touching a head to count it, whether in a crowd, at a ballot box or on a telephone list.
normalIntro.cn: 这一族词都从一个具体动作长出来：点一个头就算一个，不论是在人群里、票箱前还是电话名单上。

normal.en: Poll began as the head, and a poll of the people was a count of heads, which is why voting and surveying share the word.
normal.cn: poll 起初指「头」，a poll of the people 就是清点人头，所以投票与调查共用这个词。

normal.en: Opinion poll puts the noun after the subject it measures, and the phrase is the normal way to name a survey.
normal.cn: opinion poll 把名词放在它所测量的对象之后，是称呼民调最常用的说法。

normal.en: Go to the polls treats the word as a place or event, because the polls are where the counting happens.
normal.cn: go to the polls 把这个词当成地点或事件，因为 the polls 就是清点发生的地方。

normal.en: The verb poll takes a person or group as its object: you poll voters, students or an audience.
normal.cn: 动词 poll 以人或群体作宾语：poll voters、students、an audience。

normal.en: Pollster adds -ster, the old suffix for someone who does a thing, so the word names the person behind the numbers.
normal.cn: pollster 加了 -ster，这个古老后缀表示「做某事的人」，于是这个词指数字背后的人。

abstract.en: A word that moves from head to vote to opinion shows that public voice is always counted in bodies.
abstract.cn: 一个从「头」走到「票」再到「意见」的词说明：公共声音终究是按人头来数的。

abstract.en: The same noun can be the question, the act and the total, because a poll is a circle that closes only when the numbers come back.
abstract.cn: 同一个名词既能是问题、是行为、也是总数，因为民调是一个圈，数字回来才算闭合。

abstract.en: Counting heads is a crude measure, and the word quietly admits it: what is counted is a unit, not a mind.
abstract.cn: 数人头是一种粗糙的度量，这个词也默默承认了这一点：被数的是一个单位，而不是一个头脑。

examples.en: An opinion poll suggested that most voters wanted the plan changed.
examples.cn: 一项民意调查显示，多数选民希望这个方案作出修改。

examples.en: She polled her students about which book to read next.
examples.cn: 她就下一本读什么书征求了学生们的意见。

examples.en: The party polled forty percent of the vote.
examples.cn: 该党获得了四成选票。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「坡欧」——把人头一个个数过去，数出来的是票，问出来的是民调，都是 poll。

root: 中古荷兰语 pol（头顶、头）→ 中古英语 polle（头）→ 按人头计数 → 计票与投票 → 民意调查；属日耳曼来源，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a count of heads; from it come the vote, the tally and the place of voting, and then the modern survey and its verbs.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「清点人头」；由此分出投票、计票与投票场所，再长出当代的调查及其动词用法。

core.cn: 核心意象：一块写字板在人群里移动，一个头一个头地画勾。

branches.en: a clipboard stopped in front of a stranger
branches.cn: 写字板停在一个陌生人面前

senses.title: People of one age
senses.definition: all the people born and living at about the same time
senses.definitionCN: 大约在同一时期出生并生活的一批人
senses.example: My grandfather's generation saw great changes.

senses.why: The word first names a batch of people produced by one period.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指同一个时期「产生」出来的一批人。

senses.title: Producing
senses.definition: the act or process of producing something such as power or heat
senses.definitionCN: 生产电力、热量等事物的行为或过程
senses.example: The generation of electricity from sunlight is growing.
senses.exampleCN: 利用阳光发电正在增长。
senses.why: The original sense of begetting widened to any kind of producing.

definition_zh: 暂停；停顿；间歇；迟疑
definition_en: to stop doing something for a short time and then continue; also a short stop in speech, music or action
core_image: 悬在半空的手指：动作停住，却没有结束
scene: 录音棚里，主持人的话说到一半，抬眼看了看稿子。 The host paused in the middle of the sentence to check the script.
sceneCN: 这里是「暂停、停顿」（第 1 个义项：短暂停下再继续）；句意为主持人说到一半停下来看稿子。图中可辨识物件：话筒、稿纸、亮着的录音灯。

derivatives.zh: 由 pause 加 -ing 构成，指停顿这个动作或停住的那段时间
由 pause 与 button 复合而成，指画着两条竖线的暂停键
由拉丁词干 paus- 加 -al 构成，语音学中指「停顿处的」

senses.title: To stop for a short time
senses.definition: to stop what you are doing for a short time and then continue
senses.definitionCN: 把正在做的事短时间停下，随后继续
senses.example: The host paused in the middle of the sentence to check the script.
senses.exampleCN: 主持人说到一半停下来看稿子。
senses.why: The Greek verb pauein meant to make something stop, and English keeps that plain sense of a break that does not end the action.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语动词 pauein 意为「使停止」，英语保留了这层朴素含义：停一下，但动作并没有结束。

senses.title: A short stop in an activity
senses.definition: a short period in which an activity or a flow of speech stops
senses.definitionCN: 活动或说话流程短暂中断的那一小段时间
senses.example: After a short pause, the music started again.
senses.exampleCN: 短暂停顿之后，音乐又响起来。
senses.why: Once the verb names the act of stopping, the same form can name the gap itself, so the action becomes a measurable interval.
senses.whyCN: 动词既然能指「停」这个动作，同一个词形也能指停出来的那段空隙，动作于是变成可以计量的间歇。

senses.title: A sign holding a note longer
senses.definition: a written sign telling a performer to hold a note or rest longer than its written value
senses.definitionCN: 乐谱上要求演奏者把某个音或休止延长到超出时值的记号
senses.example: The conductor placed a pause over the final chord.
senses.exampleCN: 指挥在最后一个和弦上方标了延长记号。
senses.why: In music the idea of a deliberate hold is written down as a sign, so the word moves from a moment of time to a mark on the page.
senses.whyCN: 在音乐里，「有意停住」被写成谱面上的记号，这个词便从一段时间落到纸上的一个符号。

senses.title: To hesitate before acting
senses.definition: to wait a moment before speaking or acting because you are not sure
senses.definitionCN: 因为拿不准，在开口或行动之前先等一等
senses.example: She paused before she answered the question.
senses.exampleCN: 她回答问题之前迟疑了一下。
senses.why: A pause can be caused by doubt rather than by rest, and that hesitation is the same bodily stillness seen from the inside.
senses.whyCN: 停顿有时不是因为休息，而是因为心里拿不准；这种犹豫就是同一种身体静止，只是从内心去看它。

intro.en: Pause comes from Greek and Latin words for stopping and reached English through Old French before it was applied to music, buttons and hesitation.
intro.cn: pause 源自希腊语与拉丁语中表示「停止」的词，经古法语进入英语，后来又用于音乐、按键与犹豫。

items.en: The noun pausis meant a stopping or a rest, and it came from the verb pauein, to make something cease.
items.cn: 名词 pausis 意为停止、歇息，来自动词 pauein，即「使某事物停下」。

items.en: Latin took the Greek noun as pausa, a halt or a rest, and used it for a break in speech and in work.
items.cn: 拉丁语把希腊语名词借作 pausa，意为中止、休息，用于说话与劳作中的间歇。

items.en: Old French kept the form pause with the same sense of a stop or a rest and passed it across the Channel.
items.cn: 古法语保留 pause 这一形式，仍指停下或休息，并把它传过海峡。

items.en: Middle English pause is recorded from the fifteenth century, first in religious and learned writing, then in ordinary description of speech.
items.cn: 中古英语的 pause 自十五世纪有记录，先见于宗教与学术文字，后来用于描述日常说话。

items.en: Modern English extends pause to a printed music sign, to the button that freezes a recording, and to the hesitation before a difficult answer.
items.cn: 现代英语把 pause 扩展到乐谱记号、让录音停住的按键，以及面对难题回答前的迟疑。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the Latin and French relatives plus two words that only share the spelling or the sound; the near-meaning group gathers words for stopping and for the gap itself.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语与法语同族词，另加两个只是拼写或读音相近的词；近义组收表示停止与表示那段空隙的词。

entries.definition: The Latin noun for a halt or a rest, the source of the English word.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语名词，意为中止或休息，是英语这个词的来源。

entries.definition: Rest or quiet, built in Latin on the same root for pausing.
entries.definitionCN: 休息、安静，在拉丁语中建立在同一个表示停顿的词根上。

entries.definition: To place the body in a position, from a different Latin verb; only the spelling looks close.
entries.definitionCN: 摆出姿势，来自另一个拉丁语动词；只是拼写看上去接近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The plural of paw, an animal foot; it sounds the same but is a different word.
entries.definitionCN: paw 的复数，指动物的脚掌；读音相同，却是另一个词。

entries.definition: To end movement or action, usually for longer than a pause.
entries.definitionCN: 结束运动或动作，通常比停顿更久。

entries.definition: To stop moving, or to bring something to a stop.
entries.definitionCN: 停止移动，或使某事物停下。

entries.definition: A short period when an activity stops before it starts again.
entries.definitionCN: 活动暂停、之后重新开始的那段短时间。

entries.definition: A period of time between two events or between parts of a performance.
entries.definitionCN: 两个事件之间或演出两部分之间的时间。

normalIntro.en: The word carries a Greek verb of stopping through Latin and French, and its English life is a chain of short holds: breath, music, button, doubt.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把希腊语中表示「使停止」的动词经拉丁语和法语带进英语，它在英语里的经历是一连串短暂的停住：喘息、音乐、按键、犹豫。

normal.en: Greek pauein meant to make something stop, and pausis was the halt that came of it.
normal.cn: 希腊语 pauein 意为使某事物停下，pausis 就是由此产生的停止。

normal.en: Latin pausa and Old French pause keep almost the same shape, so the spelling barely moved on the way into English.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 pausa 与古法语 pause 形式几乎不变，所以进入英语时拼写几乎没有挪动。

normal.en: Pause for breath is the oldest kind of pause: the body cuts speech short in order to breathe.
normal.cn: pause for breath 是最古老的一种停顿：身体为了让说话中断去喘口气。

normal.en: Press pause points at the two upright bars on a player, a small picture of an action held still.
normal.cn: press pause 指播放器上那两条竖线，是把动作按住的一小幅图画。

normal.en: The verb drops the final e before -ing, so pause becomes pausing, not pauseing.
normal.cn: 动词加 -ing 时去掉词尾的 e，所以写成 pausing，而不是 pauseing。

abstract.en: A pause is proof that stopping and continuing are not opposites: the same action contains both.
abstract.cn: 停顿证明「停」与「继续」并不对立：同一个动作里两者都在。

abstract.en: Silence held for a moment can carry more weight than the words on either side of it.
abstract.cn: 被刻意留住的一小段沉默，往往比它两边的字句更有分量。

abstract.en: Every pause button assumes that what is frozen will come back, which is why the word sounds calm rather than final.
abstract.cn: 每个暂停键都预设被冻住的东西还会回来，所以这个词听起来平静，而不像终结。

examples.en: The host paused in the middle of the sentence to check the script.
examples.cn: 主持人说到一半停下来看稿子。

examples.en: There was a long pause before anyone spoke.
examples.cn: 好一阵停顿之后才有人开口。

examples.en: Pause the video when the diagram appears.
examples.cn: 图出现的时候把视频暂停一下。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泡子」——水快开时先冒一阵泡子，火候不到就再等等；pause 就是中途停一下。

root: 希腊语 pauein（使停止）→ 希腊语 pausis（停止）→ 拉丁语 pausa（中止、休息）→ 古法语 pause → 英语 pause；同族词多与「停、歇」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a short hold that leaves the action open; from it come the gap in time, the written music sign, and the hesitation of doubt.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心意象是「停住但没结束」；由此分出时间上的空隙、谱面上的延长记号，以及因拿不准而产生的迟疑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger frozen above a button, the action held but not finished.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指停在按键上方，动作被按住却没有结束。

branches.en: a speaker stopping mid-sentence
branches.cn: 说话的人在半句上停住

branches.en: the empty second after a question
branches.cn: 一个问题之后空出来的那一秒

branches.en: a printed sign above the last chord
branches.cn: 最后一个和弦上方的谱面记号

branches.en: a hand raised before an answer
branches.cn: 回答之前抬起的手

branches.en: the same stillness read once as time and once as doubt
branches.cn: 同一种静止，一处读作时间，一处读作犹豫

intro.en: A Greek root for stopping runs through the Greek noun, the Latin noun and verb, the French form, and two English endings that build new words from it.
intro.cn: 表示「停止」的希腊词根贯穿希腊语名词、拉丁语名词与动词、法语形式，以及两个由它造词的英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 确认；证实；批准；使坚定
definition_en: to show that something is true, or to make a plan or arrangement certain
core_image: 服务员在本子上把订位时间又圈了一遍
scene: 酒店前台打来电话，再次确认明天的房间。 Please confirm your booking by email.
sceneCN: 这里 confirm 指「确认」（第 1 个义项：把已有安排再核实一遍）；句意是请通过邮件确认你的预订。

derivatives.zh: 确认；证实；批准
已确认的；根深蒂固的
证实性的
再次确认

senses.title: Make an arrangement certain
senses.definition: to state that an arrangement is still true or will happen
senses.definitionCN: 说明某项安排仍然有效或将会发生
senses.example: Please confirm your booking by email.
senses.exampleCN: 请通过邮件确认你的预订。
senses.why: A plan spoken once can drift, and a second word pins it down.
senses.whyCN: 计划只说一次会飘走，再说一次才能把它钉住。

senses.title: Show that a fact is true
senses.definition: to provide evidence that a report or belief is correct
senses.definitionCN: 提供证据说明某个说法或想法是正确的
senses.example: The test confirmed his guess.
senses.exampleCN: 这次测试证实了他的猜测。
senses.why: Evidence turns a private guess into something others must accept.
senses.whyCN: 证据把私下的猜测变成别人必须接受的事实。

senses.title: Give official approval
senses.definition: to formally approve an appointment or decision
senses.definitionCN: 正式批准一项任命或决定
senses.example: The council confirmed the new plan.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会批准了新计划。
senses.why: A decision becomes final only when the proper body says yes.
senses.whyCN: 决定只有经有权机构点头，才算最终定下。

intro.en: Confirm comes from Latin confirmare, to make firm, built from com-, fully, and firmare, to strengthen.
intro.cn: confirm 来自拉丁语 confirmare，意为使坚固，由 com-（完全）与 firmare（加固）构成。

items.en: Firmus meant firm, steady and hard to move.
items.cn: firmus 意为坚固、稳定、难以推动。

items.en: Firmare meant to make something firm or secure.
items.cn: firmare 意为使某物坚固或牢靠。

items.en: Confirmare added com- to strengthen something completely.
items.cn: confirmare 加上 com-，表示把某物彻底加固。

items.en: Old French confermer carried the sense of making an agreement secure.
items.cn: 古法语 confermer 带有使约定变得牢靠的意思。

items.en: English confirm now means to prove true or to approve formally.
items.cn: 英语 confirm 如今指证明为真或正式批准。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that begin like confirm, and the meaning group names other ways of proving or approving.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 confirm 词形相近的词，近义组列出其他证明或批准的说法。

entries.definition: to behave in the way others expect
entries.definitionCN: 遵从；符合

entries.definition: to keep within limits
entries.definitionCN: 限制；禁闭

entries.definition: to discuss or give an honour
entries.definitionCN: 商议；授予

entries.definition: to check that something is true
entries.definitionCN: 核实；验证

entries.definition: to show by evidence that something is true
entries.definitionCN: 证明

entries.definition: to give formal approval to an agreement
entries.definitionCN: 正式批准

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a circled time in a notebook, then move to a lab result and to a council vote.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从本子上被圈出的时间开始，再走到实验室结果与委员会表决。

normal.en: Con- is fully and firm means solid, so to confirm is to make a thing fully solid.
normal.cn: con- 是完全，firm 是坚固，所以 confirm 就是把一件事彻底坐实。

normal.en: A confirmed booking is a booking written in pen, not pencil.
normal.cn: 确认过的预订，是用钢笔而不是铅笔写下的预订。

normal.en: A test confirms a guess the way a key confirms a lock.
normal.cn: 测试证实猜测，正如钥匙印证了锁。

normal.en: To confirm a decision is to make it stand up and stop wobbling.
normal.cn: 批准一项决定，就是让它站稳、不再摇晃。

normal.en: Say it twice and check once more, and the fact is confirmed.
normal.cn: 说两遍再核对一次，事实就确认了。

abstract.en: Picture a pen drawing a second circle around a date.
abstract.cn: 想象一支笔在一个日期外又画了一圈。

abstract.en: Picture a stamp pressed down with both hands.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚印章被双手压下去。

abstract.en: Picture a nail driven fully into wood.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗钉子被完全敲进木头。

examples.en: Could you confirm the time of the meeting?
examples.cn: 你能确认一下会议时间吗？

examples.en: Later evidence confirmed her story.
examples.cn: 后来的证据证实了她的说法。

examples.en: The board confirmed him as the new director.
examples.cn: 董事会批准他为新任主管。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 confirm 记成 con（完全）加 firm（坚固）：把一件事彻底坐实、变得牢靠，就是确认与证实。

root: 源自拉丁语 confirmare（com 完全 + firmare 加固，源自 firmus 坚固），本义是使坚固，后引申为确认、证实与批准。

sensesIntro.en: From pinning down an arrangement, to proving a fact, and finally to giving official approval.
sensesIntro.cn: 从把安排钉牢，到证明一个事实，最后到给予正式批准。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a date circled twice and a nail driven fully home.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个被圈了两遍的日期，一颗被完全敲进去的钉子。

branches.en: Confirming an arrangement removes the small doubt of a forgotten detail.
branches.cn: 确认安排，是消除「细节可能被忘」的小疑虑。

branches.en: Confirming a fact replaces belief with proof.
branches.cn: 证实事实，是用证据替换相信。

branches.en: Confirming a decision gives it the weight of an institution.
branches.cn: 批准决定，是给它加上机构的分量。

branches.en: Both senses make something stand firmer than before.
branches.cn: 两个义项都让某件事比原先站得更稳。

branches.en: Proof and approval both end a period of uncertainty.
branches.cn: 证实与批准都结束了一段不确定的时期。

intro.en: Confirm is built on Latin com-, fully, plus firmare, to make firm.
intro.cn: confirm 由拉丁语 com-（完全）与 firmare（使坚固）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin firm base also appears in firm, affirm and firmament.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的坚固词基 firm- 也出现在 firm、affirm 与 firmament 中。

items.exampleCN: 我们今天确认这份订单。

items.example: She is confirming the details now.

items.meaning: a statement that something is true
established and not likely to change
items.exampleCN: 他是一个坚定的支持者。
第二次测试是证实性的。

definition_zh: 自愿的；志愿的；无偿的；随意的；自愿做出的
definition_en: done, given, or chosen by your own free will, without being forced or paid
core_image: 自己伸出的手：没有人推，没有人付钱，是你自己决定做的
scene: 社区中心贴出新的招募海报，来往的人驻足细看。 Attendance at the evening classes is entirely voluntary.
sceneCN: 这里 voluntary 是「自愿的」（第 1 个义项：出于自由意志、不受强制）；句意是晚间课程完全凭个人意愿参加，来去自由。

pos.zh: 形容词：自愿的；志愿的；无偿的；随意的
名词：即兴独奏曲（尤指管风琴）；自愿行动者

derivatives.zh: 副词，义为「自愿地、主动地」，由形容词加副词后缀构成
名词，义为「志愿者」，与 voluntary 同出拉丁词根 voluntas
名词，义为「自愿性」，由形容词加抽象名词后缀构成
形容词，义为「不自愿的、无意的」，由否定前缀 in- 加本词构成
副词，义为「不由自主地」，由 involuntary 加副词后缀构成

senses.title: Done by free will
senses.titleCN: 自愿的：出于自己的意愿
senses.definition: done or chosen by your own decision, without being forced
senses.definitionCN: 出于自己的决定而做，不受外界强迫
senses.example: Attendance at the evening classes is entirely voluntary.
senses.exampleCN: 晚间课程完全凭个人意愿参加。
senses.why: Latin voluntas means will or wish; the adjective marks action born of one's own will.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 voluntas 意为意志、意愿；这个形容词标记「由自己的意志而生」的行动。

senses.title: Unpaid and offered
senses.titleCN: 无偿的：不取报酬的付出
senses.definition: done without payment, especially for a charitable cause
senses.definitionCN: 不取报酬地去做，尤指为公益或慈善
senses.example: She does voluntary work at the local shelter every weekend.
senses.exampleCN: 她每个周末都在当地收容所做志愿工作。
senses.why: What you will freely, you need not be paid for; giving time becomes giving it for free.
senses.whyCN: 出于自愿去做，便不要求回报，于是「自愿」延伸为「无偿」之义。

senses.title: Run by volunteers
senses.titleCN: 志愿的：由志愿者组成或运作
senses.definition: organized or staffed by people who work without pay
senses.definitionCN: 由不取报酬的人组成或运作的（组织、机构）
senses.example: The library survived thanks to the voluntary sector.
senses.exampleCN: 这家图书馆得以维持，多亏志愿部门。
senses.why: Groups of willing people form a whole sector; the adjective names that collective choice.
senses.whyCN: 许多自愿者的集合构成一个部门，形容词转而指称这种集体的自愿组织。

senses.title: Under conscious control
senses.titleCN: 随意的：受意识支配的（身体动作）
senses.definition: controlled by conscious decision of the mind, as muscles or movements
senses.definitionCN: 由意识主动控制的，如肌肉或身体动作
senses.example: Breathing is partly voluntary and partly automatic.
senses.exampleCN: 呼吸部分受意识控制，部分自动进行。
senses.why: Will governs the body's actions; movements you can choose are called voluntary.
senses.whyCN: 意志支配身体的行动，凡可由意识决定的动作即称「随意」。

senses.title: Not required by law
senses.titleCN: 非强制性的：法律或规章不做要求
senses.definition: not required by law or rules, but open to anyone who wishes
senses.definitionCN: 法律或规章不强制要求，愿意者可参与
senses.example: The company signed a voluntary code of conduct.
senses.exampleCN: 公司签署了一份自愿遵守的行为准则。
senses.why: Where force ends, will begins; what the law leaves free rests on voluntary choice.
senses.whyCN: 强制止步之处即意愿开始之处，法律不强制之事便依赖自愿选择。

senses.title: A free instrumental piece
senses.titleCN: 即兴独奏曲：尤指管风琴的自由演奏
senses.definition: a solo piece, especially for organ, played freely before or after a service
senses.definitionCN: 在礼拜前后自由演奏的独奏曲，尤指管风琴曲
senses.example: The organist opened the service with a short voluntary.
senses.exampleCN: 管风琴师以一首简短的即兴独奏曲开场。
senses.why: The player plays at will, without a set duty; freedom of will names the free piece.
senses.whyCN: 演奏者随兴而奏、无既定任务，「随意」之义转指这种自由演奏的乐曲。

intro.en: Voluntary comes from Latin voluntas, will or free choice, formed on the verb velle, to wish or to will.
intro.cn: voluntary 源自拉丁语 voluntas（意志、自愿的选择），该词由动词 velle（愿意、想要）构成。

items.en: The reconstructed root *welh₁- means to want or to choose, giving wish-words across Indo-European languages.
items.cn: 重构词根 *welh₁- 意为想要、选择，在各印欧语言中衍生出一族「意愿」词。

items.en: Velle means to wish; its noun voluntas means will, and the adjective voluntarius means of one's own will.
items.cn: 拉丁语 velle 意为愿意；名词 voluntas 意为意志，形容词 voluntarius 意为出于自己意志的。

items.en: The word passes into French as volontaire, keeping the sense of free choice.
items.cn: 该词以 volontaire 进入法语，保留自由选择之义。

items.en: English borrows voluntary in religious and legal writing, meaning done of one's own will.
items.cn: 英语在宗教与法律文本中借入 voluntary，意为出于本人意愿所为。

items.en: The senses of unpaid charitable work and of muscles under conscious control take hold.
items.cn: 17 至 19 世纪，「无偿公益」与「受意识控制的肌肉」两义确立。

items.en: Voluntary now names free choice everywhere, from voluntary work to the voluntary sector.
items.cn: 如今 voluntary 广泛指自愿之事，从志愿工作到志愿部门皆用此词。

note.en: Voluntary stands beside its Latin will-family and the opposite force-family; look-alikes share the root, near meanings share the field of willingness.
note.cn: voluntary 与拉丁「意志」词族及其反面「强制」词族相邻：形近组共享词根，近义组共享「自愿」义场。

entries.definition: a person who offers to do something without being paid
entries.definitionCN: 志愿者；与 voluntary 同出拉丁 voluntas，名词指自愿者

entries.definition: in a way done by free choice
entries.definitionCN: 自愿地；由 voluntary 加副词后缀构成

entries.definition: done against or without one's will
entries.definitionCN: 不自愿的、不由自主的；加否定前缀 in- 构成，义与本词相反

entries.definition: the principle of relying on voluntary action rather than state compulsion
entries.definitionCN: 自愿主义；由本词加 -ism 构成的学说名词

entries.definition: kind and wishing to do good
entries.definitionCN: 仁慈的、乐善的；同为 -ent/-lent 结尾，但词根是 velle 的另一形式 bene velle（愿意好），词族相关而拼写相异

entries.definition: ready and happy to do something
entries.definitionCN: 愿意的、乐意的；日耳曼词源，强调乐意的态度

entries.definition: available if you want it, but not required
entries.definitionCN: 可选择的、非强制的；侧重「可选」，不侧重「无偿」

entries.definition: done or kept without payment
entries.definitionCN: 无报酬的；只描述无酬，不强调意愿

entries.definition: happening naturally, without being planned
entries.definitionCN: 自发的；强调未经计划，voluntary 强调自由决定

entries.definition: required by a rule or law
entries.definitionCN: 强制的、义务的；与本词构成直接反义对照

normalIntro.en: Five anchors from the Latin will-family of voluntas and velle.
normalIntro.cn: 五个锚点，全部来自拉丁语 voluntas（意志）与 velle（愿意）词族。

normal.en: velle means to wish; voluntary means done by your own wish.
normal.cn: velle 意为愿意；voluntary 就是「按自己的意愿做」。

normal.en: volunteer is the person form: one who offers freely.
normal.cn: volunteer 是它的「人」形：主动报名、不计报酬的人。

normal.en: involuntary adds the negative in-, meaning against your will.
normal.cn: involuntary 加否定前缀 in-，意为「违背意愿、不由自主」。

normal.en: voluntarily is simply voluntary in action: doing it by choice.
normal.cn: voluntarily 就是 voluntary 的动作版：自愿地去做。

normal.en: the word sits inside voluntary sector, the world of unpaid help.
normal.cn: 这个词就住在 voluntary sector（志愿部门）里，即无偿奉献的世界。

abstract.en: Imagine a hand reaching out on its own, pushed by nobody and paid by nobody.
abstract.cn: 想象一只自己伸出的手，无人推动，无人付钱。

abstract.en: Two doors stand open: one says forced, one says chosen; you walk through the second.
abstract.cn: 两扇门都开着：一扇写着强制，一扇写着自愿；你走向第二扇。

abstract.en: A will like a small engine inside the chest, starting the action before anyone asks.
abstract.cn: 意志像胸中一台小引擎，不等任何人开口就先发动了行动。

examples.en: He joined the rescue team on a purely voluntary basis.
examples.cn: 他完全出于自愿加入了救援队。

examples.en: The hospital relies heavily on voluntary donations.
examples.cn: 这家医院在很大程度上依赖志愿捐助。

examples.en: Smiling is usually voluntary, but laughter often is not.
examples.cn: 微笑通常是随意的，大笑却往往身不由己。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我乐于停」——我乐于停下被强迫的脚步，自己选择去做，这才是自愿。谐音只是记忆钩子，词源仍来自拉丁 voluntas（意志）。

root: 拉丁语 velle（愿意）+ 名词 voluntas（意志）+ 形容词后缀 -arius 构成 voluntarius，经古法语 volontaire 进入英语。同根词还有 volunteer、benevolent（bene 好 + velle）、malevolent（male 坏 + velle）等，「意愿」一族。

sensesIntro.en: From the will outward: free choice, free giving, volunteer groups, the body's chosen movements, and the free piece of music.
sensesIntro.cn: 从意愿向外铺开：自由选择、无偿付出、志愿组织、身体受控的动作，最后到随兴的乐曲。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one act of will, from inner wish outward to free action
core.cn: 核心意象：同一次「意愿」，从内心的想延伸到自由的做

branches.en: The root sense: acting by your own decision
branches.cn: 根本义：按自己的决定行动

branches.en: Willingness without wages: charity and the volunteer sector
branches.cn: 不取报酬的意愿：公益与志愿部门

branches.en: Will applied to the body: movements under conscious control
branches.cn: 意志作用于身体：受意识支配的动作

branches.en: Where law stays silent, will fills the gap
branches.cn: 法律沉默之处，由意愿来填补

branches.en: Playing at will becomes the free musical piece
branches.cn: 随兴而奏，便成为自由的乐曲

intro.en: The Latin will-verbs velle and its noun voluntas spread through prefixes of good, bad, and negation.
intro.cn: 拉丁语意愿动词 velle 及其名词 voluntas，借助「好、坏、否定」等前缀铺成一族词。

latinIntro.en: In Latin, velle built a family of words about wishing well, ill, or freely.
latinIntro.cn: 在拉丁语中，velle 构成了一族关于「愿好、愿坏、愿自便」的词。

derivatives.zh: 自愿地，由 voluntary 加副词后缀构成
志愿者，与 voluntary 同根的名词
不自愿的，由 in- 加 voluntary 构成

definition_zh: 瓦片；瓷砖；地砖；（纸）牌；铺瓦；贴砖
definition_en: a flat thin piece used to cover roofs, walls or floors, or to cover a surface with such pieces
core_image: 一片片平薄的方块，紧密相扣盖住屋顶或地面
scene: 台风过后屋顶漏雨，父亲爬上梯子查看。 He lifted a cracked tile and showed it to me.
sceneCN: 这里 tile 是「瓦片」（第 1 个义项：盖屋顶的平薄块材）；句意：他掀起一片碎瓦给我看。

pos.zh: 瓦片；瓷砖；地砖；（麻将等）牌

derivatives.zh: tile 加 -ing，义为「铺砖；铺瓦；（总称）瓷砖」
tile 加 -er，义为「铺瓦工；贴砖工」
roof + tile 复合，义为「屋顶瓦」

senses.title: A flat piece for roofs
senses.definition: a thin curved or flat block of baked clay, slate or concrete used to cover a roof
senses.definitionCN: 陶土、石板或混凝土制成的薄平块，用以覆盖屋顶
senses.example: Wind dislodged several tiles from the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 大风掀掉了屋顶的几片瓦。
senses.why: The core image is thin slabs lapped like scales over a roof frame.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是如鳞片般层层搭叠盖住屋架的薄块。

senses.title: A flat piece for walls or floors
senses.definition: a flat square of ceramic, stone or glass used to cover bathroom walls or floors
senses.definitionCN: 陶瓷、石材或玻璃的方形薄块，用于铺贴浴室墙面或地面
senses.example: The kitchen floor is covered in blue tiles.
senses.exampleCN: 厨房地面铺着蓝瓷砖。
senses.why: The same lapped or grouted squares move indoors from the roof.
senses.whyCN: 同样的方块从屋顶移进室内，以缝勾连。

senses.title: A rectangular piece in some games
senses.definition: a small flat block used in games such as mahjong or dominoes, marked with symbols
senses.definitionCN: 麻将、多米诺等游戏中印有符号的小薄块
senses.example: She drew the winning tile at mahjong.
senses.exampleCN: 她打麻将时摸到了制胜的牌。
senses.why: A small flat marked block behaves like a decorative tile in play.
senses.whyCN: 印着符号的小薄块在游戏中如同一枚可摆弄的瓷砖。

senses.title: To cover a surface with tiles
senses.definition: to cover a roof, wall or floor with tiles fitted edge to edge
senses.definitionCN: 用瓷砖或瓦片边靠边覆盖屋顶、墙面或地面
senses.example: They tiled the shower walls on Saturday.
senses.exampleCN: 他们周六给淋浴间墙面贴了砖。
senses.why: The noun names the covering piece, then the act of assembling it.
senses.whyCN: 名词先指覆盖之块，再指将其拼合的动作。

senses.title: A hat, in old slang
senses.definition: an informal old word for a hat, used in earlier English speech
senses.definitionCN: 旧时口语中对帽子的诙谐称呼
senses.example: He tipped his tile as he entered, said the old novel.
senses.exampleCN: 那本旧小说里写道：他进门时抬了抬帽檐。
senses.why: A hat sits flat on the head as a tile sits on a roof.
senses.whyCN: 帽子平扣头顶，正如瓦片平覆屋顶。

senses.title: Tiled tightly: densely packed
senses.definition: arranged so closely that no gaps remain between the pieces
senses.definitionCN: 排布紧密，块与块之间不留缝隙
senses.example: The map was tiled with tiny photographs.
senses.exampleCN: 整张地图密密铺满了小照片。
senses.why: Tiling is the pattern of perfect packing, the zero-gap arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 铺砖即完美拼合的范式：零空隙的排布。

senses.title: A tiled window or area on screen
senses.definition: a section of a computer screen divided into equal blocks without overlap
senses.definitionCN: 计算机屏幕被分成互不重叠的等块
senses.example: Tile the two documents side by side on screen.
senses.exampleCN: 把两个文档在屏幕上平铺并排。
senses.why: Equal blocks fitted edge to edge copy the mason's wall of tiles.
senses.whyCN: 屏幕等块边靠边拼合，复制了砖工的砖墙。

senses.title: A tile on a phone or app grid
senses.definition: a rectangular icon block on a phone or website start screen that updates with information
senses.definitionCN: 手机或网页起始屏上的矩形图标块，可随信息更新
senses.example: The weather tile shows tomorrow's rain.
senses.exampleCN: 天气磁贴显示明天的雨。
senses.why: The grid block inherits both the shape and the close packing of a tile.
senses.whyCN: 界面磁贴继承了瓷砖的形状与密铺逻辑。

intro.en: Tile comes from the Old English tigele, a roof tile, from the Latin tegula, itself from tegere, to cover. It is a direct Latin loan into Germanic speech: a tile is simply a cover in pieces.
intro.cn: tile 源自古英语 tigele「屋瓦」，借自拉丁语 tegula，后者出自动词 tegere「覆盖」。这是拉丁语进入日耳曼语的直接借词：tile 的本义就是「分块的覆盖物」。

items.en: The reconstructed root (s)teg- meant to cover, as in thatch of Germanic stock.
items.cn: 重构词根 (s)teg- 意为覆盖，与日耳曼语的 thatch 同源。

items.en: Tegula meant a roofing tile, from tegere, to cover.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tegula 指屋瓦，源出 tegere「覆盖」。

items.en: Tigele arrived with Roman roofing craft and settled in English.
items.cn: 古英语 tigele 随罗马屋瓦工艺进入英语。

items.en: Tile spread to wall and floor pieces as glazed squares appeared.
items.cn: 随着釉面方块出现，tile 扩展到墙面与地面块材。

items.en: The gaming sense for dominoes and mahjong blocks was recorded.
items.cn: 多米诺与麻将块的「牌」义见于记载。

items.en: Modern computing reused tile for screen blocks and app grids.
items.cn: 现代计算界面把 tile 用于屏幕分块与应用磁贴。

note.en: The first group gathers the cover-root family; the second lists nearby flat-piece words.
note.cn: 第一组是「覆盖」词根家族；第二组列出相邻的薄片块材词。

entries.definition: roof covering of straw, from the same Indo-European cover root
entries.definitionCN: 茅草屋顶，与 tile 同出「覆盖」词根

entries.definition: to cover and guard, built on the Latin teg- root
entries.definitionCN: 保护，建立于拉丁 teg- 词根

entries.definition: to fasten with cord; spelled close but unrelated
entries.definitionCN: 系、绑；拼写相近而词源无关

entries.definition: a large thick flat piece of stone or concrete
entries.definitionCN: 大而厚的平板石材

entries.definition: a small roof piece laid in overlapping rows
entries.definitionCN: 层层搭叠的小型屋面板

entries.definition: a block for walls, thicker than a tile
entries.definitionCN: 砌墙的块材，比砖厚

normalIntro.en: Real links: tile from Latin cover, roof tile, ceramic tiles, tile the screen, and the tiler's trade.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：tile 源自拉丁「覆盖」、roof tile、ceramic tiles、tile the screen，以及铺砖工的行当。

normal.en: Tile and protect share one Latin root: to cover.
normal.cn: tile 与 protect 同出拉丁词根：覆盖。

normal.en: Roof tiles lap like scales to shed the rain.
normal.cn: 屋瓦如鳞片搭叠，把雨水卸走。

normal.en: Ceramic tiles leave thin grout lines between blocks.
normal.cn: 瓷砖块间只留细缝勾缝。

normal.en: Tiling a screen means equal blocks with zero overlap.
normal.cn: 平铺屏幕就是等块、零重叠。

normal.en: A tiler is the person who makes the surface whole, piece by piece.
normal.cn: 铺砖工把表面逐块拼成整体。

abstract.en: A whole surface is an agreement among many small squares.
abstract.cn: 完整的表面是许多小方块的彼此约定。

abstract.en: Covering is protection arranged in repeatable pieces.
abstract.cn: 覆盖是以可重复的块材实现的保护。

abstract.en: Order on screens borrows order from the mason's wall.
abstract.cn: 屏幕上的秩序借自砌砖的秩序。

examples.en: The bathroom was retiled in white and green.
examples.cn: 浴室重新铺了白色和绿色瓷砖。

examples.en: A loose tile clattered down into the gutter.
examples.cn: 一片松动的瓦哐当落进檐槽。

examples.en: Dominoes are really just tiles with dots.
examples.cn: 多米诺骨牌其实就是带点的牌块。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「踢楼」——瓦片松动会掉下来「踢」到「楼」下的人，快去修 → tile 瓦片；瓷砖

root: 拉丁语 tegere「覆盖」→ tegula「屋瓦」→ 古英语 tigele → tile；与 protect、thatch 同出一源，核心是「成块覆盖」。

sensesIntro.en: The covering piece travels from roofs to floors, to game blocks, to verbs, to screen regions and app icons.
sensesIntro.cn: 这块「覆盖之片」从屋顶走到地面、走进游戏、化为动词，又登上屏幕成为分区与磁贴。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: thin flat blocks lapped or fitted to cover without gaps.
core.cn: 核心意象：薄平块搭叠拼合，无缝覆盖。

branches.en: Roof and room share the same covering piece.
branches.cn: 屋顶与屋内共用同一种覆盖块。

branches.en: The marked block enters play.
branches.cn: 印符号的块进入游戏。

branches.en: The noun becomes the covering action.
branches.cn: 名词化作覆盖的动作。

branches.en: The hat sits like a tile; packing reaches zero gaps.
branches.cn: 帽子如瓦平扣；密铺臻于无缝。

branches.en: Screens adopt the grid of tiles.
branches.cn: 屏幕采纳了瓷砖的网格。

intro.cn: tile 的拉丁「覆盖」词根在 protect 等词中清晰可见；词条展示行业词与复合形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin cognates come from tegere, to cover.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同源词出自 tegere「覆盖」。

the Roman roofing tile, the direct ancestor

items.exampleCN: 罗马瓦片仍见于发掘现场。

items.example: The tiler finished the hall today.

A rooftile cracked in the frost.
The floor tiles click under your shoes.

items.meaning: a screen region in a tiled layout

He counted the mahjong tiles in his hand.

definition_zh: 步速；速度；节奏；进度；踱步
definition_en: the speed at which a person or an animal moves, the rate at which an activity develops, or the act of walking back and forth
core_image: 跑道上一个人的步子均匀落下，鞋底一次次压在同一条白线上
scene: 跑道边的教练握着一块秒表，眼睛盯着从弯道冲出来的选手。 The runner held a steady pace over the final lap.
sceneCN: 这里的 pace 是「步速、速度」（第 1 个义项：移动的快慢）；句意为这名选手在最后一圈保持了稳定的速度。图中可辨识物件：秒表、弯道、白线。

derivatives.zh: 由 pace 加表示「做某事的人或物」的 -er 构成，义为「领跑者；定速器」
由 pace 与 maker 复合而成，义为「领跑者；心脏起搏器」
由 pace 与 setter 复合而成，义为「定步速的人；带头人」

senses.title: The speed at which someone moves
senses.definition: the speed at which a person or an animal walks, runs or otherwise moves
senses.definitionCN: 人或动物行走、奔跑或移动的快慢
senses.example: The runner held a steady pace over the final lap.
senses.exampleCN: 这名选手在最后一圈保持了稳定的速度。
senses.why: Pace began as the Latin word for a single step, so the noun first counted steps on the ground; only later did it come to mean how fast those steps follow one another.
senses.whyCN: pace 起初是拉丁语中表示「一步」的词，所以这个名词最早数的是地上的步子；至于「步子迈得多快」，是后来才长出来的意思。

senses.title: The rate at which something develops
senses.definition: the speed at which an activity, a process or a period of time moves forward
senses.definitionCN: 活动、过程或一段时间向前推进的快慢
senses.example: The pace of change in the industry has surprised everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 这个行业变化的速度让所有人都感到意外。
senses.why: Once the word measured how quickly feet cover ground, it could measure how quickly anything else moves, so trade, study and daily life all acquired a pace of their own.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词能量出双脚走完一段路的快慢，它就能量出别的任何事物推进的快慢，于是贸易、学业与日常生活都有了自己的节奏。

senses.title: To walk back and forth
senses.definition: to walk with regular steps across a room or a small area, especially while waiting or worrying
senses.definitionCN: 在一个房间或一小片地方来回走动，尤指等待或焦虑时
senses.example: He paced the corridor while the interview went on.
senses.exampleCN: 面试进行时，他在走廊里来回踱步。
senses.why: Since a step is the unit that pace counts, the verb simply names the act of taking steps; with no destination in view, those steps turn into restless walking to and fro.
senses.whyCN: 既然「一步」是 pace 所计的单位，动词自然就指迈步这件事；当眼前没有目的地时，这些步子就变成了焦躁的来回走动。

intro.en: Pace comes from Latin passus, a step, which itself grew out of pandere, to stretch out; French passed the word to English in the Middle Ages, first as a step and later as a rate of movement.
intro.cn: pace 来自拉丁语 passus（一步），而 passus 又出自 pandere（伸开）；中世纪时法语把这个词传给英语，先指一步，后指移动的快慢。

items.en: Pandere meant to spread or stretch out, and a leg stretching forward across the ground is the picture behind the whole family.
items.cn: pandere 意为展开、伸开，一条腿向前跨过地面，正是这一族词背后的画面。

items.en: Passus named a step or a stride, and Roman surveyors also used it for a fixed measure of length counted in double steps.
items.cn: passus 指一步或一个跨步，罗马的测量者也用它作固定的长度单位，按双步计算。

items.en: Old French kept the noun as pas, a step, and built a verb meaning to step or to walk.
items.cn: 古法语把这个名词保留为 pas（一步），并造出表示迈步、行走的动词。

items.en: English borrowed pace in the thirteenth century for a step and for the length of a step, and the sense of speed followed from timing those steps.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入 pace，指一步以及一步的长度；等到人们开始给这些步子计时，速度义就跟着出现了。

items.en: Modern English uses pace for walking speed, for the rhythm of any activity, and as a verb for walking to and fro.
items.cn: 现代英语用 pace 指步速、任何活动的节奏，也用作动词表示来回走动。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the Latin step or on the English word itself; the near-meaning group collects words for speed and rhythm.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「步」之上或由这个词本身构成的词；近义组收表示速度与节奏的词。

entries.definition: To go past something, or a narrow way through mountains.
entries.definitionCN: 经过某物，或山间通道；同出拉丁语 passus。

entries.definition: A way through, or a short part of a text.
entries.definitionCN: 通道；也指文章的一小段。

entries.definition: A person who sets the speed for runners, or a device that regulates the heart.
entries.definitionCN: 为跑者定速的人，或调节心跳的装置。

entries.definition: A person or group whose rate others try to match.
entries.definitionCN: 步速领先、被别人追赶的人或团体。

entries.definition: How fast something moves, measured in distance over time.
entries.definitionCN: 事物移动的快慢，按单位时间走过的距离衡量。

entries.definition: A measure of how often or how fast something happens.
entries.definitionCN: 衡量某事发生频率或快慢的尺度。

entries.definition: The speed of a piece of music or of an activity.
entries.definitionCN: 乐曲或活动的速度。

entries.definition: Speed in a particular direction, a term used in physics.
entries.definitionCN: 沿特定方向的速度，物理学用语。

normalIntro.en: Pace keeps the picture of a single step on the ground, and every later meaning is that step repeated at a certain rate.
normalIntro.cn: pace 始终保留「地上落下的一步」这个画面，后来的一切含义都是这一步以某种快慢重复下去。

normal.en: Pace goes back to Latin passus, a step, so the word began as something you could count on the ground.
normal.cn: pace 上溯拉丁语 passus（一步），所以它最初是地上数得出来的东西。

normal.en: Keep pace with keeps that picture: two people taking steps at the same rate, so neither falls behind.
normal.cn: keep pace with 保留了这个画面：两个人以同样的快慢迈步，谁也不会落后。

normal.en: A pacemaker was first a person who set the speed for a runner, and the same word now names the device that sets the rhythm of a heart.
normal.cn: pacemaker 最初指为跑者定速的人，如今同一个词也指给心脏定节奏的装置。

normal.en: Speed and pace are close, but pace often suggests a rhythm held over time, while speed is simply how fast something goes.
normal.cn: speed 与 pace 意思很近，但 pace 常暗示一段时间里维持住的节奏，而 speed 只是单纯有多快。

normal.en: French pas still means a step, which is why the two words look so alike.
normal.cn: 法语 pas 至今仍指一步，这正是两个词看起来如此相似的原因。

abstract.en: A word that started as one footfall suggests that all speed is finally a matter of repeated steps, one after another.
abstract.cn: 一个从一声脚步开始的词说明：一切速度最终都不过是一步接一步的重复。

abstract.en: To keep pace is to agree to move at someone else's rhythm, which is why the phrase sounds like a relationship and not only a measurement.
abstract.cn: 跟上步伐就是同意按别人的节奏移动，所以这个说法听起来像一种关系，而不只是一次测量。

abstract.en: A man pacing a corridor is measuring time with his feet, since waiting has no clock but does have steps.
abstract.cn: 在走廊里踱步的人其实在用脚量时间，因为等待没有钟表，却有一步步的移动。

examples.en: The runner held a steady pace over the final lap.
examples.cn: 这名选手在最后一圈保持了稳定的速度。

examples.en: The pace of change in the industry has surprised everyone.
examples.cn: 这个行业变化的速度让所有人都感到意外。

examples.en: He paced the corridor while the interview went on.
examples.cn: 面试进行时，他在走廊里来回踱步。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「配斯」——配斯在跑道上踩着均匀的步子，一步接一步；记住 pace 是步速、节奏。

root: 来自拉丁语 passus（一步），再上溯 pandere（伸开），经古法语 pas 进入英语；同族词多与「跨步、通过」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is one step repeated; the senses divide into the speed of those steps, the rhythm any activity takes on, and the restless walking of someone with nowhere to go.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是反复落下的一步；义项按「这些步子的快慢」「任何活动获得的节奏」「无处可去时的来回走动」分出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: even footfalls on a running track, each sole pressing the same white line.
core.cn: 核心意象：跑道上一声声均匀的脚步，鞋底一次次压在同一条白线上。

branches.en: a runner holding the same speed to the line
branches.cn: 一直保持同一速度跑到终点的选手

branches.en: a measured length of ground in a surveyor's book
branches.cn: 测量员本子上量出的一段地

branches.en: an office where the work keeps speeding up
branches.cn: 工作不断加速的一间办公室

branches.en: a corridor worn thin by waiting feet
branches.cn: 被等待的脚步磨薄的一条走廊

branches.en: one word for a daily rhythm and for restless steps
branches.cn: 同一个词，既指日常节奏，也指不安的踱步

intro.en: The word is built on a Latin noun for a step and a Latin verb for stretching out, then passed through French with a noun ending that English did not need to change.
intro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语表示「一步」的名词与表示「伸开」的动词之上，再经法语传来，英语几乎不必改动它的形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin passus and pandere are both recorded, so this word has a reliable Latin ancestry.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 passus 与 pandere 均有记录，因此这个词有可靠的拉丁语世系。

items.meaning: one who sets or holds the speed
a leader in speed or a heart device

definition_zh: 坚韧的；艰苦的；强硬的；顽强的
definition_en: strong and not easily broken, broken down, or defeated
core_image: 扯不断的旧牛皮：越拽越显出它的韧劲
scene: 教练看着坚持跑完全程的队员说： That was a tough race, but you finished it!
sceneCN: 这里 tough 是「艰苦的」（第 2 个义项：费力、难熬的）；句意是教练称赞队员跑完了这场艰难的比赛。

pos.zh: 坚韧的；艰苦的；强硬的；粗暴的

derivatives.zh: 由 tough 加 -ness 构成，义为「坚韧；顽强」
由 tough 加 -en 构成，义为「使坚韧；使强硬」

senses.title: Strong and hard to break
senses.definition: physically strong and difficult to cut, tear, or chew
senses.definitionCN: 物理上结实，难以切割、撕扯或咀嚼
senses.example: The meat was so tough that I couldn't chew it.
senses.exampleCN: 这肉太老了，我嚼不动。
senses.why: The core image of oxhide resists every pull, hence hard to break.
senses.whyCN: 牛皮意象抗拒一切拉扯，故本义即「不易破坏」。

senses.title: Difficult and demanding
senses.definition: difficult to do or endure; requiring effort and endurance
senses.definitionCN: 难以完成或承受的，需要努力与忍耐
senses.example: It was a tough year for the whole industry.
senses.exampleCN: 对整个行业来说，这是艰难的一年。
senses.why: What resists the body also resists plans and feelings.
senses.whyCN: 抗拒身体之物同样抗拒计划与情绪，故引申为「艰难」。

senses.title: Strict and unyielding
senses.definition: firm and not willing to soften, as with rules or people
senses.definitionCN: 坚定不让步的，指规则或人的态度
senses.example: The city adopted tough new traffic laws.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市出台了严格的新交通法规。
senses.why: A will that resists bending is described with the same word as leather.
senses.whyCN: 不肯弯折的意志与拽不断的皮革用同一个词形容。

senses.title: Rough or violent
senses.definition: behaving in a rough, aggressive way
senses.definitionCN: 举止粗鲁、好斗的
senses.example: He grew up on the tough streets of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 他在城市里粗粝的街头长大。
senses.why: Hardness of material turns into hardness of manner.
senses.whyCN: 材质的硬转为作风的硬。

intro.en: Tough is an Old English word from the Germanic family, originally describing oxhide-like durability.
intro.cn: tough 是古英语日耳曼词，最初形容如牛皮般耐用之物。

items.en: The root *denk- meant 'to chew', linking toughness with chewing resistance.
items.cn: 词根 *denk- 意为「咀嚼」，把「韧」与嚼不动相连。

items.en: *Tanhuzaz described things hard to chew or break.
items.cn: 日耳曼重构形 *tanhuzaz 形容难嚼难折之物。

items.en: Tōh meant tough, tenacious, or sticky.
items.cn: 古英语 tōh 意为坚韧、粘韧。

items.en: Spelling settled as tough; the sense widened to difficulty and severity.
items.cn: 中古英语拼写定型为 tough，词义扩展到艰难与严厉。

items.en: All four senses stay in active use today.
items.cn: 四个义项沿用至今。

note.en: Spelling neighbors of tough and words of the endurance field.
note.cn: 与 tough 拼写相近的词及同属耐力义场的词。

entries.definition: not smooth; violent
entries.definitionCN: 粗糙的；粗暴的，与 tough 音近且部分义重合，词源不同

entries.definition: to force air out of the lungs noisily
entries.definitionCN: 咳嗽，拼写只差首字母，词源无关

entries.definition: to make tough
entries.definitionCN: 使坚韧，由 tough 加 -en 构成

entries.definition: although; however
entries.definitionCN: 虽然；不过，拼写近似而词源无关

entries.definition: solid, difficult, or severe
entries.definitionCN: 硬的；难的；严厉的，与 tough 多义重合

entries.definition: able to spring back after pressure
entries.definitionCN: 有韧性的；恢复快的，强调回弹

entries.definition: strongly built
entries.definitionCN: 结实的；强健的，强调构造牢固

entries.definition: easily broken
entries.definitionCN: 易碎的；脆弱的，tough 的反义对照

normalIntro.en: Fix tough with the oxhide picture and the -ough family.
normalIntro.cn: 用牛皮画面和 -ough 词族拼写来固定 tough。

normal.en: the -ough in tough sounds like /ʌf/
normal.cn: tough 的 -ough 读 /ʌf/，与 rough、cough 同韵

normal.en: tough luck = bad luck
normal.cn: tough luck（倒霉）是口语同情或调侃语

normal.en: a tough nut to crack = a hard problem
normal.cn: tough nut to crack（难啃的骨头）指难题

normal.en: toughen up = become stronger
normal.cn: toughen up（变强韧）用于锻炼与磨砺

normal.en: tough meat needs slow cooking
normal.cn: 肉 tough（老）就小火慢炖，本义最直观

abstract.en: Pull an old leather strap until your arms give up
abstract.cn: 拉扯旧皮带直到双臂认输，韧劲即 tough

abstract.en: Climb a hill that pushes back with every step
abstract.cn: 爬一座步步回推的山坡，即艰难的 tough

abstract.en: Meet a rule that refuses to bend
abstract.cn: 遇上一条不肯弯折的规则，即强硬的 tough

examples.en: It was a tough decision, but the right one.
examples.cn: 这是个艰难的决定，但也是正确的决定。

examples.en: Tough leather lasts for decades.
examples.cn: 坚韧的皮革能用几十年。

examples.en: The police took a tough line on drunk driving.
examples.cn: 警方对酒驾采取强硬态度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「塔夫」——想象耐磨的「塔夫绸」布料，扯不断、揉不烂，正合 tough 的韧劲。

root: 古英语 tōh（坚韧），出日耳曼语族；印欧词根 *denk-（咀嚼）的重构关联：嚼不动的东西即「韧」。与 rough 词源不同，仅韵近。

sensesIntro.en: One leather-strong word covers hard material, hard times, hard rules, and hard streets.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个「如皮革般强韧」的词，覆盖了硬物、难境、铁律与粗粝街头。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: oxhide that refuses every pull
core.cn: 核心意象：拒绝一切拉扯的牛皮

branches.en: material that resists cutting and chewing
branches.cn: 抗拒切割与咀嚼的材质

branches.en: circumstances that resist effort
branches.cn: 抗拒努力的境况

branches.en: rules and wills that resist bending
branches.cn: 抗拒弯折的规则与意志

branches.en: manners hardened into roughness
branches.cn: 硬化为粗暴的作风

branches.en: one resistance, many battlefields
branches.cn: 同一种抵抗，不同的战场

intro.en: Tough is a bare Germanic adjective that freely takes native suffixes.
intro.cn: tough 是不带前缀的日耳曼形容词，可自由加本土后缀。

latinIntro.en: Being Germanic, tough has no Latin relatives.
latinIntro.cn: 作为日耳曼词，tough 没有拉丁同族词。

items.example: the last exam item was a toughie
items.exampleCN: 考卷最后一题是道难题

definition_zh: 完全地；充分地；整整
definition_en: completely, in detail, or at least a stated amount
core_image: 开关被推到最大，指示灯全亮
scene: 她完全明白这个决定的分量。 She was fully aware of the weight of the decision.
sceneCN: 这里 fully 是「完全地」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她完全明白这个决定的分量。

derivatives.zh: 满的；完全的
满；充分

senses.title: Completely
senses.definition: completely, with nothing missing or doubtful
senses.definitionCN: 完全地，没有遗漏或疑问
senses.example: She was fully aware of the weight of the decision.
senses.exampleCN: 她完全明白这个决定的分量。
senses.why: This is the main adverb sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是副词的主要义项。

senses.title: In full detail
senses.definition: in a complete or detailed way
senses.definitionCN: 以完整或详细的方式
senses.example: The plan was fully explained to us.
senses.exampleCN: 计划向我们做了充分说明。
senses.why: Fullness can apply to explanation.
senses.whyCN: 「满」也可以用于说明。

senses.title: At least
senses.definition: at least a stated amount
senses.definitionCN: 至少达到所述数量
senses.example: It is fully five miles from here.
senses.exampleCN: 离这里足足有五英里。
senses.why: This older sense marks a full measure.
senses.whyCN: 这个较旧的义项标记一个完整的量。

intro.en: Fully is full with the adverb suffix -ly.
intro.cn: fully 是 full 加副词后缀 -ly。

items.en: Full meant filled or complete.
items.cn: full 意为装满的或完整的。

items.en: The adverb form fully appeared.
items.cn: 副词形式 fully 出现。

items.en: It meant in a complete way.
items.cn: 它意为以完全的方式。

items.en: It described detailed explanation.
items.cn: 它描述详细的说明。

items.en: It also marked a full amount.
items.cn: 它也标记一个完整的数量。

note.en: Fully is compared with look-alike words and words for completeness.
note.cn: 把 fully 与形近词以及表示完全的词作比较。

entries.definitionCN: 满的

entries.definition: a young female horse

entries.definition: very strong anger
entries.definitionCN: 狂怒

entries.definition: in every way
entries.definitionCN: 完全地

entries.definition: wholly

entries.definition: completely
entries.definitionCN: 彻底地

normalIntro.en: Fully means the whole amount, with nothing held back.
normalIntro.cn: fully 意为全部的量，毫无保留。

normal.en: She was fully aware of the weight of the decision.
normal.cn: 她完全明白这个决定的分量。

normal.en: The plan was fully explained to us.
normal.cn: 计划向我们做了充分说明。

normal.en: It is fully five miles from here.
normal.cn: 离这里足足有五英里。

normal.en: The machine is fully automatic.
normal.cn: 这台机器是全自动的。

normal.en: The puppies are fully grown.
normal.cn: 这些小狗已经长大。

abstract.en: To understand fully is to have no corner left in shadow.
abstract.cn: 完全理解就是没有角落留在阴影里。

abstract.en: A fully open door invites both exit and entry.
abstract.cn: 完全敞开的门同时允许离开和进入。

abstract.en: Some truths are only fully seen from far away.
abstract.cn: 有些真相只有从远处才能完全看清。

examples.en: She was fully aware of the weight of the decision.
examples.cn: 她完全明白这个决定的分量。

examples.en: The plan was fully explained to us.
examples.cn: 计划向我们做了充分说明。

examples.en: The machine is fully automatic.
examples.cn: 这台机器是全自动的。

dict_mnemonic.text: fully = full（满的）+ -ly（……地）；常与 aware、understand、prepared 搭配，表示「完全、充分」。

sensesIntro.en: Fully means completely, in full detail, or a full stated amount.
