core.en: The whole amount, with nothing left out.
core.cn: 全部的量，毫无遗漏。

branches.en: A mind takes in every fact.
branches.cn: 头脑接收每个事实。

branches.en: An explanation covers every step.
branches.cn: 说明涵盖每一步。

branches.en: A distance reaches a full measure.
branches.cn: 距离达到完整的量。

branches.en: Complete knowledge and complete detail belong together.
branches.cn: 完整的认识与完整的细节彼此相属。

branches.en: Degree and amount both reach the limit.
branches.cn: 程度与数量都达到上限。

intro.en: Fully builds phrases for complete states.
intro.cn: fully 构成表示完整状态的短语。

latinIntro.en: The base is Germanic; only the suffix is English.
latinIntro.cn: 词基属日耳曼语；后缀属英语。

items.example: The fullness of the moon was beautiful.
He was fully aware of the risk.

definition_zh: 辩论；争论；斟酌
definition_en: a formal discussion in which two sides argue for opposing views
core_image: 两排人隔着长桌来回交锋
scene: 议会里两派人为预算争了一整个下午。 The two sides will debate the budget again tomorrow.
sceneCN: 这里 debate 指「辩论」（第 1 个义项：正式的对立讨论）；句意是两派明天再辩预算。

derivatives.zh: 辩论者
有争议的
辩论活动
未经辩论的

senses.title: Formal argument between two sides
senses.definition: an organised discussion in which two sides defend opposite views
senses.definitionCN: 两种立场各持一方、有秩序地进行的讨论
senses.example: The two sides will debate the budget again tomorrow.
senses.exampleCN: 两派明天将再次就预算展开辩论。
senses.why: Two claims meet in public and each must answer the other.
senses.whyCN: 两种主张当众相遇，谁都得回答对方。

senses.title: A long argument among people
senses.definition: a serious argument among people who disagree
senses.definitionCN: 意见不同的人之间较真的争吵
senses.example: The plan caused a heated debate at the dinner table.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划在饭桌上引起了一场激烈的争论。
senses.why: Even without a chair or a rule book, people still take sides.
senses.whyCN: 就算没有主席和规则，人们照样会分成两边。

senses.title: To weigh a choice in the mind
senses.definition: to turn a choice over and over before deciding
senses.definitionCN: 在下决心之前反复掂量一个选择
senses.example: She debated whether to call him that night.
senses.exampleCN: 她那晚反复斟酌要不要打电话给他。
senses.why: A private argument is still a debate, held inside one head.
senses.whyCN: 一个人的内心争辩，也是一场辩论，只是发生在脑袋里。

intro.en: Debate came from Old French debatre, to fight or contend, built on Latin battuere, to beat.
intro.cn: debate 来自古法语 debatre（争斗），根源是拉丁语 battuere（击打）。

items.en: Battuere meant to beat or strike with a weapon.
items.cn: battuere 指用武器击打。

items.en: Debatre meant to struggle, with words as often as with arms.
items.cn: debatre 指争斗，用嘴和用兵器一样常见。

items.en: Debate entered English as both a quarrel and a formal argument.
items.cn: debate 进入英语时，既指争吵也指正式辩论。

items.en: Parliament gave the word its ordered, public sense.
items.cn: 议会赋予这个词有秩序、公开进行的含义。

items.en: Debate also means to weigh a private choice.
items.cn: 如今 debate 也指在心里掂量一个选择。

note.en: The look-alike group all carry a sharp middle sound, and the meaning group runs from calm talk to open dispute.
note.cn: 形近组中间都有一个清亮的音，近义组则从平和的商谈走到公开的争端。

entries.definition: money taken out of an account
entries.definitionCN: 从账户里支出的钱

entries.definition: money paid back after a purchase
entries.definitionCN: 购物之后退回的钱

entries.definition: money that you owe
entries.definitionCN: 欠别人的钱

entries.definition: to talk about something with others
entries.definitionCN: 与别人一起谈论某事

entries.definition: to speak angrily because you disagree
entries.definitionCN: 因为意见不同而带火气地说话

entries.definition: a serious disagreement that lasts
entries.definitionCN: 持续较久的严重分歧

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with two rows of speakers and end with one person arguing inside his own head.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从两排发言的人开始，落到一个人在自己脑子里争辩。

normal.en: A debate needs two sides, or it is only a speech.
normal.cn: 辩论得有两边，否则只是一场演讲。

normal.en: The stronger claim is the one that can answer back.
normal.cn: 更强的那个主张，是能回应对手的那个。

normal.en: Rules do not end the anger; they only keep it in chairs.
normal.cn: 规则不能消掉火气，只把火气按在椅子上。

normal.en: At dinner the debate begins over the salt and ends over politics.
normal.cn: 饭桌上的争论从盐罐开始，到政治结束。

normal.en: A mind that debates itself has two good speakers.
normal.cn: 在心里自我辩论的人，有两个好辩手。

abstract.en: Picture two hands raised at the same moment in a hall.
abstract.cn: 想象大厅里两只手在同一刻举起。

abstract.en: Picture a table where the same sentence is said twice, louder.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子上，同一句话被说了两遍，一遍比一遍响。

abstract.en: Picture a man walking home arguing with someone who is not there.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人走回家，一路和不在场的人争辩。

examples.en: The two sides will debate the budget again tomorrow.
examples.cn: 两派明天将再次就预算展开辩论。

examples.en: Her decision caused a heated debate among the staff.
examples.cn: 她的决定在员工中引起了激烈争论。

examples.en: He debated for a long time before answering.
examples.cn: 他斟酌了很久才回答。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 debate 记成「对掰」：de 是相对，bate 像 bat（球拍），两边各拿一块拍子来回对打，就是辩论。

root: 经古法语 debatre（争斗）进入英语，更早来自拉丁语 battuere（击打），所以辩论本来带着「交手」的意味。十四世纪入英语时兼指争吵与正式论辩，十六世纪议会用它指有秩序的公开讨论，现代又添了在心里反复权衡的意思。

sensesIntro.en: From two sides striking with words, to an argument at dinner, to a choice weighed alone.
sensesIntro.cn: 从两边用言语交手，到饭桌上的争吵，再到独自掂量一个选择。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two rows of people trading blows with words across a table.
core.cn: 核心意象：两排人隔着桌子，用言语来回交手。

branches.en: The first sense is the ordered contest, watched by a room.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是有秩序的较量，满屋的人看着。

branches.en: Take away the rules and the same contest becomes a quarrel.
branches.cn: 拿掉规则，同一场较量就成了争吵。

branches.en: The contest turns inward when one person holds both sides.
branches.cn: 当一个人同时站在两边，较量就转向了内心。

branches.en: Both are people disagreeing; only the setting has changed.
branches.cn: 两者都是人在意见相左，只是场合不同。

branches.en: A loud argument and a silent one share the same shape.
branches.cn: 大声的争吵和无声的争辩，形状是一样的。

intro.en: Debate has a short family: the person, the quality of being open to question, and a few fixed compounds.
intro.cn: debate 这一族很短：辩论的人、可争议的性质，还有几个固定搭配。

latinIntro.en: The Latin element is battuere, to beat; the modern word keeps the idea of verbal blows.
latinIntro.cn: 其中的拉丁成分是 battuere（击打），现代词仍保留言语交手的意味。

items.meaning: to argue formally or weigh a choice
items.example: They debate every Friday in the club.
items.exampleCN: 他们每周五在社团里辩论。

items.meaning: a person who argues in a debate
items.example: She is the best debater in her class.
items.exampleCN: 她是班上最会辩论的人。

items.example: Whether the plan will work is debatable.
items.exampleCN: 这个计划是否行得通还有争议。
这项动议未经辩论就通过了。

items.meaning: a group that competes in argument
items.example: Our debate team won the regional final.
items.exampleCN: 我们的辩论队赢了地区决赛。

items.meaning: a club where members practise arguing
items.example: The debate club meets on Wednesdays.
The council held an open debate on the plan.
items.exampleCN: 委员会就这个计划举行了公开辩论。

definition_zh: 事先；预先；提前；事前
definition_en: earlier than a particular time, event, or action; in advance
core_image: 事情还没发生，手已经先伸到前面去了：把准备做在时间的前头
scene: 开会前她把资料全都打印装订好了，等大家到场就能直接讨论，一点不慌乱。 She prepared all the documents beforehand, so the meeting went smoothly.
sceneCN: 这里 beforehand 是「事先、预先」（第 1 个义项：早于某个时间或事件发生）；句意是她在会议开始之前就把资料准备好了，因此会议进行得很顺利。

derivatives.zh: 由「after（之后）+ hand」构成的对应词，义为「事后」（罕用，多见于早期英语）
由 beforehand 加名词后缀构成的罕用名词，义为「预先性；提前状态」
相关近义词，义为「前进；预先」（in advance 短语与 beforehand 同义）

senses.title: Earlier than a particular time or event
senses.titleCN: 事先；在某个时间或事件之前
senses.definition: at an earlier time than something happens or is done
senses.definitionCN: 在事情发生或完成之前的时间点上
senses.example: She prepared all the documents beforehand.
senses.exampleCN: 她事先把所有文件都准备好了。
senses.why: The compound joins before with hand, as if time were held and handled before the moment arrives.
senses.whyCN: 复合词把 before（在前）和 hand（手）组合起来，仿佛时间被握在手里、先一步递到事情发生之前。

senses.title: In advance, as a preparation
senses.definition: in advance so that one is ready when the time comes
senses.definitionCN: 提前安排妥当，等到关键时刻不至于手忙脚乱
senses.example: If you book the tickets beforehand, you will pay less.
senses.exampleCN: 如果你提前订票，价格会便宜一些。
senses.why: Doing the work in advance shifts effort from the busy moment to the calm one before it.
senses.whyCN: 把功夫下在前头，等于把忙碌时刻的工作挪到之前从容的时段里完成。

senses.title: Before doing something else, as a first step
senses.definition: as a prior step before moving on to something else
senses.definitionCN: 作为先行的步骤，把某事处理完再谈下一步
senses.example: Read the contract beforehand before you sign it.
senses.exampleCN: 签字之前要先读一遍合同。
senses.why: The word marks sequence: one action must be handled ahead of another.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标记先后顺序：一件事必须先于另一件事处理。

senses.title: Ahead of other people, earlier than others
senses.definition: earlier than other people manage to do or know something
senses.definitionCN: 在别人之前完成或了解到某事
senses.example: He knew the result beforehand because he had seen the list.
senses.exampleCN: 他提前知道了结果，因为他看过名单。
senses.why: Being ahead in time also means being ahead of everyone else who waits.
senses.whyCN: 在时间上领先，也意味着领先于那些还在等待的人。

senses.title: With advance knowledge or notice
senses.titleCN: 预先获知；事先得到消息
senses.definition: with knowledge of something before it is announced or happens
senses.definitionCN: 在事情公布或发生之前就已知晓
senses.example: Nobody told me beforehand that the plan had changed.
senses.exampleCN: 事先没有人告诉我计划变了。
senses.why: Information received early lets a person act as if the future were already in hand.
senses.whyCN: 提前拿到信息，就像把未来的事情先握在手里一样。

senses.title: In prior arrangement or agreement
senses.definition: as something arranged or agreed before the occasion itself
senses.definitionCN: 指在正式场合之前就已经谈好、定好的安排
senses.example: We had agreed beforehand to split the cost equally.
senses.exampleCN: 我们事先说好了平摊费用。
senses.why: An agreement made ahead binds both sides before the event arrives.
senses.whyCN: 事先达成的约定在事情到来之前就已约束双方。

senses.title: Anticipating future needs, planning ahead
senses.titleCN: 未雨绸缪地；为将来打算
senses.definition: with thought given to future needs before they arise
senses.definitionCN: 在需求出现之前就预作打算
senses.example: Thinking beforehand about possible problems saved the team a lot of trouble.
senses.exampleCN: 提前考虑可能出现的问题，为团队省去了很多麻烦。
senses.why: The mind reaches forward in time, handling tomorrow's tasks today.
senses.whyCN: 思绪提前伸向未来，把明天的事拿到今天来处理。

senses.title: In negative and interrogative uses, impossibility of prior knowledge
senses.titleCN: 用于否定或疑问：无法事先知道
senses.definition: used to say that something could not be known or done in advance
senses.definitionCN: 常用于否定句或疑问句，表示某事无法预先知道或做到
senses.example: I could not have known beforehand that the flight would be cancelled.
senses.exampleCN: 我事先不可能知道航班会被取消。
senses.why: Negation flips the image: the hand did not reach forward, so surprise follows.
senses.whyCN: 否定翻转了意象：手没有先伸出去，于是意外接踵而来。

intro.en: Beforehand is a native English compound of before plus hand, formed within Middle English and parallel to the rarer afterhand.
intro.cn: beforehand 是英语本土复合词，由 before（在前）加 hand（手）构成，形成于中古英语时期，与罕用的 afterhand（事后）相对应。

items.en: Before comes from Old English beforan, itself be- (by, about) plus foran (in front of), a spatial word later extended to time.
items.cn: before 源自古英语 beforan，由 be-（在、关于）加 foran（在前方）构成，原本表示空间方位，后来引申为时间上的先后。

items.en: Hand is a common Germanic noun, Old English hand, found in many compound expressions for possession and action.
items.cn: hand 是常见的日耳曼语名词，古英语作 hand，在英语中大量出现于表示掌握、动作的复合表达里。

items.en: The compound beforehand is first recorded in the late fourteenth century, meaning at an earlier point or in front.
items.cn: 复合词 beforehand 最早见于十四世纪晚期，意为「在更早的时点；在前方」。

items.en: The sense narrows to in advance, in anticipation, and the word settles into its modern adverbial use alongside the rare parallel afterhand.
items.cn: 词义逐渐收窄为「提前、预先」，该词固定为现代副词用法，与罕用的对应词 afterhand（事后）并存。

items.en: Today beforehand is the standard adverb for doing or knowing something in advance, common in both everyday and formal contexts.
items.cn: 如今 beforehand 是表示「事先、预先」的标准副词，日常与正式语体中都十分常用。

note.en: The first group gathers words built from the same before- and fore- material; the second gathers near-synonymous ways of saying in advance.
note.cn: 第一组收录由 before-、fore- 等相同材料构成的词；第二组收录表示「提前、预先」的近义说法。

entries.definition: a stroke made with the palm of the hand facing forward; shares the -hand element but means a forward hand position, not time
entries.definitionCN: 正手；与 beforehand 共享 -hand 成分，但指手掌朝前的击球方式，与时间无关，只是构词相近。

entries.definition: a system of quick writing using symbols; ends in -hand like beforehand but refers to a shortened hand method, not time
entries.definitionCN: 速记；与 beforehand 一样以 -hand 结尾，但指缩略的书写方法，只是构词方式相似，词义不同。

entries.definition: the rare mirror compound meaning afterward; built with -hand exactly like beforehand but pointing the other way in time
entries.definitionCN: 事后（罕用）；与 beforehand 用同样方式以 -hand 构成的镜像词，只是时间方向相反。

entries.definition: ahead of the time when something happens; the common phrase-level equivalent of beforehand
entries.definitionCN: 提前；beforehand 最常见的短语级同义表达。

entries.definition: too early, before the proper time; adds a nuance of being earlier than is right
entries.definitionCN: 过早地；提前得不止一步而是过了头，带有不合时宜的贬义色彩。

entries.definition: earlier than the expected or required time
entries.definitionCN: 比预期或要求的时间早；与 beforehand 同义而更口语化。

normalIntro.en: The five associations below build on the real compound before plus hand.
normalIntro.cn: 以下五条联想都基于真实的复合结构 before（在前）加 hand（手）。

normal.en: before + hand: your hand reaches before the moment arrives
normal.cn: before 加 hand：手先伸到时刻到来之前

normal.en: beforehand and afterhand are a pair, one ahead and one behind
normal.cn: beforehand 与 afterhand 是一对，一个在前一个在后

normal.en: before itself is be- plus foran, in front
normal.cn: before 本身由 be- 加 foran 构成，义为在前方

normal.en: same family: before, beforelong, beforehand all point earlier in time
normal.cn: 同族词：before、beforelong、beforehand 都指向更早的时间

normal.en: collocation anchor: know beforehand, plan beforehand, prepare beforehand
normal.cn: 搭配锚点：know beforehand（事先知道）、plan beforehand（预先计划）、prepare beforehand（提前准备）

abstract.en: Picture posting the letter a day before the deadline, the queue already behind you
abstract.cn: 想象在截止日前一天就把信寄出，队伍还没排起来你已办完

abstract.en: Feel the calm of a packed suitcase by the door the night before travel
abstract.cn: 感受出发前夜行李箱已收好立在门边的那份从容

abstract.en: Imagine holding tomorrow in your hand today
abstract.cn: 想象今天就把明天握在手里

examples.en: If you book the tickets beforehand, you will pay less.
examples.cn: 如果你提前订票，价格会便宜一些。

examples.en: Nobody told me beforehand that the plan had changed.
examples.cn: 事先没有人告诉我计划变了。

examples.en: The notice arrived late, so there was no time to prepare.
examples.cn: 通知来得很晚，根本没时间准备。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「必福汉德」——必先福在手：福气要先握在手里，事情就能顺利，正如 beforehand 强调事先把一切安排妥当。

root: 英语本土复合词：before（源自古英语 beforan，be- 加 foran「在前」）+ hand（古英语 hand「手」），十四世纪晚期合成，义为「在事前、提前」，与罕用的 afterhand（事后）相对应。

sensesIntro.en: From the core image of reaching ahead in time, the senses move from simple priority to preparation, prior knowledge, prior agreement, and the negative case of not knowing in advance.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「把手伸到时间前头」的核心意象出发，义项由单纯的时间领先，扩展到预先准备、预先知情、事先约定，以及否定用法中的「无法预知」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the hand reaching before the moment, doing and knowing ahead of time
core.cn: 核心意象：手伸到时刻到来之前，把事情先做好、先知道

branches.en: Sheer time priority, ahead of the event or of other people
branches.cn: 单纯的时间领先，早于事件或早于他人

branches.en: Preparation done in advance so the moment goes smoothly
branches.cn: 提前做好准备，让关键时刻从容不迫

branches.en: Prior steps and agreements that bind before the occasion
branches.cn: 先行步骤与事先约定，在场合到来之前就定好

branches.en: Advance knowledge and its failure, knowing or not knowing in advance
branches.cn: 预先知情及其反面，知道或无法事先知道

branches.en: Anticipatory planning for future needs
branches.cn: 为将来需求预作打算的远虑

intro.en: Beforehand is a compound, not an affixed word, so the items below cover its building blocks and the parallel time-words formed the same way.
intro.cn: beforehand 是复合词而非派生词，因此下列条目介绍它的构件，以及按同样方式构成的时间类平行词。

latinIntro.en: English has no Latin root here, but Latin ante (before) and manus (hand) offer classical parallels to the two parts of the compound.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语词根，但拉丁语 ante（在前）与 manus（手）恰好对应复合词的两个部分，可作古典参照。

items.meaning: the hand, used figuratively for control or action
items.example: The matter is in hand now.
items.exampleCN: 这件事现在已在处理之中。

items.example: The garden is beflowered in spring.
Check the forecast before you sail.

items.exampleCN: 后来我们谈起了这件事。

items.meaning: to see something before it happens
items.example: No one could foresee the delay.
items.exampleCN: 没人能预见到这次延误。

latinEntries.exampleCN: ante meridiem 意为中午之前。

latinEntries.example: Manuscript originally meant written by hand.
latinEntries.exampleCN: manuscript 一词原义是用手写成。

derivatives.zh: 由 fore-（预先）加 knowledge（知识）构成，义为「预知；预知能力」
由 fore-（预先）加 thought（思考）构成，义为「深谋远虑；预先考虑」

definition_zh: 前提；前提假设；（复数）房屋及场地；法律文书开头陈述的事实；以……为前提预先提出
definition_en: a statement accepted as true and used as the basis of an argument, or (in the plural) a building and its land
core_image: 长桌的四条桌腿先稳稳立住，桌面上才摆得下一层层叠起的论证卡片
scene: 辩论开始前，主持人提醒双方先确认共同接受的基本判断，否则后面的推论都无处落脚。 The whole argument rests on a premise that nobody has tested.
sceneCN: 这里指论证所依据的基本判断（第 1 个义项：作为论证基础的前提命题）；句意为整个论证都建立在一个无人检验过的前提上；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 前提；前提假设；（复数）房屋及场地
以……为前提预先提出（较少用）

derivatives.zh: 复数形式，义为「房屋及场地；营业场所」
由动词加已然词尾构成，义为「以……为基础的」
逻辑学中的另一种拼写，义同「前提」
由「前提」与「基于」复合而成，义为「以前提为基础的」

senses.title: A proposition that supports an argument
senses.definition: a statement put forward as true so that a conclusion can be drawn from it
senses.definitionCN: 作为真实陈述提出、以便从中推出结论的命题
senses.example: The main premise of the essay is that prices reflect information.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章的主要前提是价格反映信息。
senses.why: The Latin word meant something sent before, and this sense places the statement ahead of the conclusion.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁词本义是「事先送出之物」，这一义项把它放在结论之前。

senses.title: An assumption taken without proof
senses.titleCN: 未加证明就接受的假设
senses.definition: a belief that a study or person accepts as true without testing it
senses.definitionCN: 研究或个人未经检验就当作真实的信念
senses.example: The model works only if its premise about human rationality holds.
senses.exampleCN: 只有当模型关于人类理性的假设成立时，它才有效。
senses.why: What is put before an argument is often simply granted, which is how a premise becomes an assumption.
senses.whyCN: 放在论证之前的东西常被直接认可，「前提」由此变成「假设」。

senses.title: The major premise of a syllogism
senses.definition: the general statement from which a syllogism begins, before the minor premise is applied
senses.definitionCN: 三段论起始的一般性陈述，在其后接上小前提
senses.example: The major premise says all mammals are warm-blooded.
senses.exampleCN: 大前提说所有哺乳动物都是温血的。
senses.why: Logic gave the word a fixed slot: the general claim sits first, and the specific case is placed under it.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学给这个词一个固定位置：一般性主张坐第一，具体事例被置于其下。

senses.title: The minor premise of a syllogism
senses.definition: the specific statement that brings a particular case under the general one
senses.definitionCN: 把具体事例归入一般陈述之下的特定陈述
senses.example: The minor premise states that this animal is a mammal.
senses.exampleCN: 小前提陈述这只动物是哺乳动物。
senses.why: The second slot in the syllogism is also called a premise, since both statements must be granted before the conclusion.
senses.whyCN: 三段论中的第二个位置同样称为前提，因为两个陈述都必须先被认可，结论才成立。

senses.title: A building and its land
senses.definition: the buildings and the ground belonging to a business or an owner, used in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 属于某企业或业主的建筑物与土地，用复数形式
senses.example: The inspectors walked through the factory premises.
senses.exampleCN: 检查人员走遍了工厂的场地。
senses.why: Legal deeds opened by describing the property set before the reader, and that list of property became the buildings themselves.
senses.whyCN: 法律契约开头先描述摆在读者面前的财产，这份财产清单后来就指建筑物本身。

senses.title: The property recited in a deed
senses.titleCN: 法律文书开头陈述的财产
senses.definition: the opening part of a legal instrument that sets out the facts and property concerned
senses.definitionCN: 法律文书开头说明相关事实与财产的部分
senses.example: The lease recites the premises before stating the rent.
senses.exampleCN: 这份租约在说明租金之前先陈述标的财产。
senses.why: The word names what is placed in front of the operative clauses, so it labels that opening recital.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指放在操作性条款之前的内容，因此用来指开头的陈述部分。

senses.title: A condition treated as given
senses.titleCN: 模型中当作给定的条件
senses.definition: a condition that a model or calculation accepts as fixed before it begins
senses.definitionCN: 模型或计算在开始之前就当作固定条件的设定
senses.example: The estimate rests on the premise that fuel prices stay flat.
senses.exampleCN: 这一估算建立在燃料价格持平的假设之上。
senses.why: A model must fix something before it can move, and whatever is fixed is literally placed in front.
senses.whyCN: 模型必须先固定某些东西才能运转，被固定者正被摆在最前面。

senses.title: A claim a debate must grant
senses.titleCN: 辩论中须先接受的主张
senses.definition: a statement that one side asks the other to accept before the exchange can proceed
senses.definitionCN: 一方要求另一方在交锋开始前先接受的主张
senses.example: The judge asked whether both sides shared that premise.
senses.exampleCN: 主持人问双方是否共有那个前提。
senses.why: Debate is an argument built in public, so it needs a floor of agreed statements under it.
senses.whyCN: 辩论是当众搭建的论证，因此需要一层公认陈述作地板。

senses.title: To state something beforehand
senses.definition: to set something out in advance as a basis for what follows
senses.definitionCN: 事先把某内容摆出来，作为后续论述的基础
senses.example: Let me premise my answer with one condition.
senses.exampleCN: 请允许我先以一个条件作为回答的前提。
senses.why: The verb kept the Latin sense of sending something ahead, and English uses it rarely, mostly in formal prose.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了拉丁语「事先送出」的意思，英语中很少用，多见于正式书面语。

intro.en: Premise comes from Latin praemissa, things sent before, from praemittere, to send ahead. Logic took the word for the statements placed before a conclusion, and law took it for the property described at the start of a deed; the plural then became the buildings themselves.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 praemissa「事先送出之物」，出自动词「预先送出」。逻辑学用它指放在结论之前的陈述，法律用它指契约开头描述的财产，其复数随后就指建筑物本身。

items.en: Mittere meant to send or let go, and it stands behind words of sending, such as mission and transmit.
items.cn: 这个词根意为「送、放出」，英语中表示发送的词多出自它。

items.en: The prefix prae- added «in front», so the verb meant to send something ahead of what follows.
items.cn: 前缀加上「在前」，于是动词意为把某物先于后续内容送出去。

items.en: The neuter plural named the things set before a conclusion, and logic adopted it as a technical term.
items.cn: 中性复数指放在结论之前的内容，逻辑学把它采用为术语。

items.en: Translations of Aristotle fixed major and minor premise as the two statements above and below the conclusion.
items.cn: 对亚里士多德著作的翻译固定了「大前提」与「小前提」，即结论之上与之下的两个陈述。

items.en: Deeds opened by reciting the property, and the plural premises came to mean that property and then the buildings on it.
items.cn: 契约开头先陈述财产，复数形式便指该财产，随后又指其上的建筑物。

items.en: The building sense now lives almost entirely in the plural, while the logic sense keeps the singular; the split's exact date is uncertain.
items.cn: 建筑物义如今几乎只存在于复数，逻辑义则保留单数；两者分开的确切年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the same Latin root or looks close; the second group names other starting points of reasoning.
note.cn: 第一组共享同一拉丁词根或形近；第二组指推理的其他起点。

entries.definition: The plural noun for a building and its land, from the property clause of a deed.
entries.definitionCN: 指房屋及场地，来自契约中的财产条款。

entries.definition: Based on a stated assumption; the past participle used as an adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 指以某陈述假设为基础的，是过去分词作形容词。

entries.definition: The older spelling used in logic for a stated proposition.
entries.definitionCN: 逻辑学中指前提命题的旧拼写。

entries.definition: First in rank; it belongs to the Latin word for first, not to sending ahead.
entries.definitionCN: 指地位最高的；属于拉丁语「第一」，与「预先送出」无关。

entries.definition: A bonus or an insurance payment; it comes from the word for reward.
entries.definitionCN: 指奖金或保险费；来自表示报酬的词。

entries.definition: A declaration that one will do something; its root is to send forth a word, a different verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指表示将做某事的声明；其词根是「送出话语」，属另一动词。

entries.definition: Something accepted as true without evidence, often silently.
entries.definitionCN: 指无证据而被接受为真的东西，常是默许的。

entries.definition: A belief that must already hold for a statement to make sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个陈述要成立就必须先已存在的信念。

entries.definition: A statement that can be judged true or false.
entries.definitionCN: 指可判断真假的陈述。

entries.definition: A tentative explanation offered for testing, not merely granted.
entries.definitionCN: 指提出来供检验的暂时解释，而不只是被认可。

entries.definition: A principle accepted without proof as a starting point.
entries.definitionCN: 指无需证明即被接受作为出发点的原理。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the table-leg picture, the syllogism slots, the legal deed and the everyday plural.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用桌腿画面、三段论的两个位置、法律契约与日常复数用法。

normal.en: A premise is sent before the conclusion, just as a table leg is placed before the table top.
normal.cn: 前提先于结论送出，正如桌腿先于桌面立好。

normal.en: The major premise is the wide statement; the minor premise puts one case under it.
normal.cn: 大前提是宽的一般陈述，小前提把一个事例放到它下面。

normal.en: Premises in the plural are buildings, from the property clause at the head of a deed.
normal.cn: 复数形式指建筑物，来自契约开头的财产条款。

normal.en: A false premise makes a valid argument reach a wrong conclusion.
normal.cn: 前提错了，形式有效的论证也会得出错误结论。

normal.en: On the premise that is the everyday phrase that carries the logic sense into ordinary writing.
normal.cn: 「以……为前提」是把逻辑义带入日常写作的固定说法。

abstract.en: A premise is a floor that nobody looks at until the argument falls through it.
abstract.cn: 前提是一块地板，直到论证掉了下去，才有人低头看它。

abstract.en: Every model stands on statements it never proves, and that silence is what makes it usable.
abstract.cn: 每个模型都站在它从不证明的陈述上，正是这份沉默让它可用。

abstract.en: The same word can name a sentence and a building, because both are things set in front of you.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既能指一句话，也能指一栋楼，因为两者都是摆在你面前的东西。

examples.en: The study rests on the premise that memory declines with age.
examples.cn: 这项研究建立在记忆随年龄衰退这一前提上。

examples.en: If the premise is false, the conclusion cannot stand.
examples.cn: 如果前提错误，结论就站不住。

examples.en: Visitors must not smoke anywhere on the premises.
examples.cn: 访客不得在场地内任何地方吸烟。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「普瑞密斯」——「普」通人先「密」密接受的那句话，就是推理的前提

root: 拉丁语 praemissa「事先送出之物」← praemittere「预先送出」= prae-「在前」+ mittere「送、放」。逻辑学经中世纪翻译固定「大前提、小前提」，法律契约开头的财产陈述引申出「房屋及场地」。十五世纪起见于英语；两义分化的确切年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses run from logic to property: a supporting proposition, an untested assumption, the major and minor premises, buildings and land, a deed recital, a fixed model condition, a debated claim, and the rare verb.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从逻辑延伸到财产：支撑命题、未验证假设、大前提、小前提、房屋场地、契约陈述、模型条件、辩论主张，以及少用的动词义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: four legs are set down first, and only then can the stacked cards of argument rest on the top.
core.cn: 核心意象：先放下四条桌腿，论证的卡片堆才放得上桌面。

branches.en: THE ARGUMENT FLOOR: the proposition that must be granted before debate can proceed.
branches.cn: 论证的地板：辩论开始前必须先被认可的那个命题。

branches.en: THE UNPROVED GRANT: assumptions that a person or a model simply accepts.
branches.cn: 未经证明的认可：人或模型直接接受的假设。

branches.en: THE TWO LOGIC SLOTS: the general statement and the case placed under it.
branches.cn: 逻辑的两个位置：一般陈述与置于其下的事例。

branches.en: THE LEGAL PROPERTY: the recited property and the buildings standing on it.
branches.cn: 法律上的财产：契约陈述的财产及其上的建筑物。

branches.en: THE RARE VERB: to send a condition ahead as a basis.
branches.cn: 少用的动词义：事先把一个条件送出作为基础。

intro.en: Premise is a Latin participle turned noun, and the same root that sends things ahead also produced words of mission and transmission.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语分词转成的名词，同一个「预先送出」词根也产生了「使命」「传送」等词。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies praemittere and praemissa; the logic and property senses both grew from the idea of things placed in front.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「预先送出」与「事先送出之物」；逻辑义与财产义都从「摆在前面之物」长出来。

items.example: It marks what is sent ahead.
items.exampleCN: 它标出事先送出的东西。

items.example: The root of mission and transmit.
items.exampleCN: 这是「使命」与「传送」的词根。

items.example: The direct source of the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这是该名词的直接来源。

items.example: It became the logic term for a premise.
It marks the rare English verb premise.
items.exampleCN: 它标明这个少用的英语动词。

items.example: The legal sense moved into everyday property talk.
items.exampleCN: 法律义进入日常财产用语。

items.meaning: a statement set before a conclusion
items.example: The everyday singular that carries the logic sense.
items.exampleCN: 这是承载逻辑义的日常单数形式。

items.example: It survives chiefly in British academic prose.
items.exampleCN: 它主要保留在英国学术写作中。

derivatives.zh: 复数形式，义为「房屋及场地」
加已然词尾，义为「以……为基础的」
逻辑学旧拼写，义为「前提」
复合形容词，义为「以前提为基础的」

definition_zh: 核的；原子核的；核能的；细胞核的
definition_en: relating to a nucleus, especially the atomic nucleus or the cell nucleus
core_image: 一个极小的中心，周围绕着一圈电子或一层膜
scene: 这个国家大部分电力来自核电站。 The country gets most of its electricity from nuclear power plants.
sceneCN: 这里 nuclear 指「核能的」（第 2 个义项：由原子核反应释放能量的）；句意：该国大部分电力来自核电站；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 核的；原子核的；核能的；核武器的；细胞核的；核心家庭的

derivatives.zh: 核；原子核；细胞核
核动力的
无核的
具备核能力的
核工程学（少用）

senses.title: Of the atomic nucleus
senses.definition: relating to the nucleus of an atom
senses.definitionCN: 与原子核有关的
senses.example: Nuclear size is measured in femtometres.
senses.exampleCN: 原子核的尺度以飞米计。
senses.why: The adjective simply attaches the noun nucleus to atomic physics, where the centre of the atom is the object of study.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把 nucleus 直接接到原子物理上，那里研究的对象就是原子的中心。

senses.title: Nuclear energy
senses.definition: describing energy released by changes in atomic nuclei
senses.definitionCN: 指由原子核变化释放的能量
senses.example: Nuclear power supplies a fifth of the country's electricity.
senses.exampleCN: 核电供应全国五分之一的电力。
senses.why: Because the energy comes from the nucleus rather than from chemical bonds, the adjective names the source of the power.
senses.whyCN: 因为能量来自原子核而不是化学键，这个形容词命名的就是能量的来源。

senses.title: Nuclear weapons
senses.definition: describing weapons whose explosive force comes from nuclear reactions
senses.definitionCN: 指爆炸力来自核反应的武器
senses.example: The treaty limits the number of nuclear warheads.
senses.exampleCN: 该条约限制核弹头的数量。
senses.why: The same source of energy, released deliberately and instantly, yields a weapon, so the adjective marks the mechanism of the blast.
senses.whyCN: 同一种能量来源若被有意瞬间释放，就成为武器，因此这个形容词标出爆炸的机制。

senses.title: Nuclear physics
senses.definition: relating to the branch of physics that studies nuclei and their reactions
senses.definitionCN: 与研究核及其反应的物理分支有关
senses.example: Nuclear physics grew out of radioactivity research.
senses.exampleCN: 核物理学从放射性研究中发展出来。
senses.why: A discipline named after its object takes the adjective as a fixed modifier, as in nuclear physics or nuclear chemistry.
senses.whyCN: 以研究对象命名的学科会把形容词作为固定修饰语，如 nuclear physics 或 nuclear chemistry。

senses.title: Of the cell nucleus
senses.definition: relating to the nucleus of a living cell
senses.definitionCN: 与活细胞的细胞核有关的
senses.example: Nuclear DNA is separated from the cytoplasm by a membrane.
senses.exampleCN: 核 DNA 由一层膜与细胞质隔开。
senses.why: Biology uses the same adjective for the cell's centre, and compounds such as nuclear envelope keep the two senses distinct by context.
senses.whyCN: 生物学用同一个形容词指细胞的中心，nuclear envelope 等复合词靠上下文把两个义项区分开。

senses.title: Nuclear family
senses.definition: describing a household of parents and their dependent children
senses.definitionCN: 指由父母与其未成年子女组成的家庭
senses.example: The survey compared nuclear and extended households.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查比较了核心家庭与大家庭。
senses.why: Social science borrowed the image of a small centre with close members, contrasting it with the wider extended family.
senses.whyCN: 社会科学借用「小核心加紧密成员」的意象，用来与更宽的扩展家庭相对照。

senses.title: Nuclear medicine
senses.definition: describing medical techniques that use radioactive substances
senses.definitionCN: 指使用放射性物质的医学技术
senses.example: Nuclear medicine scans reveal how an organ is working.
senses.exampleCN: 核医学扫描能显示器官的工作状况。
senses.why: Radioactive tracers are read by their nuclear emissions, so the medical branch is named after the physical process.
senses.whyCN: 放射性示踪剂靠其核辐射被读取，因此这个医学分支按物理过程命名。

senses.title: Nuclear envelope
senses.definition: describing the membrane that surrounds the cell nucleus
senses.definitionCN: 指包围细胞核的那层膜
senses.example: The nuclear envelope breaks down during mitosis.
senses.exampleCN: 核膜在有丝分裂过程中解体。
senses.why: An anatomical compound uses the adjective to say which structure the membrane belongs to.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学复合词用这个形容词说明这层膜属于哪个结构。

senses.title: Figurative extreme option
senses.definition: in politics, describing an extreme measure reserved as a last resort
senses.definitionCN: 政治语境中指留作最后手段的极端措施
senses.example: Both sides avoided the nuclear option in the talks.
senses.exampleCN: 双方在谈判中都避免使用极端手段。
senses.why: The destructive power of nuclear weapons supplies a metaphor for any step that would end the game.
senses.whyCN: 核武器的破坏力为任何「一出手就终结局面」的步骤提供了比喻。

intro.en: Nuclear is the adjective of nucleus, formed with -ar; its history splits between atomic physics and cell biology.
intro.cn: nuclear 是 nucleus 的形容词，由 -ar 构成；它的历史分为原子物理与细胞生物学两条线。

items.en: Nucleus, diminutive of nux 'nut', meant a kernel. English borrowed the noun in the 17th century.
items.cn: nucleus 是 nux「坚果」的指小形式，意为果仁。英语在 17 世纪借入这个名词。

items.en: The adjective nuclear is recorded in the 19th century in general senses such as 'relating to a kernel or centre'. The precise first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 形容词 nuclear 在 19 世纪有「与果核或中心有关的」这类一般义。确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Robert Brown's nucleus gave biology its own central body, and nuclear later described the structures around it.
items.cn: Robert Brown 的 nucleus 为生物学提供了自己的中心小体，nuclear 后来用于描述它周围的结构。

items.en: Rutherford's model placed nearly all atomic mass in a tiny nucleus, and nuclear physics was born around 1911 to 1912.
items.cn: 卢瑟福的模型把原子几乎全部质量放进一个极小的核，核物理学约在 1911 至 1912 年诞生。

items.en: The nuclear age fixed the word in public language through weapons and power stations, adding figurative uses such as the nuclear option.
items.cn: 1945 年之后的核时代通过武器与电站把这个词固定进公共语言，并增加了「极端手段」这类比喻用法。

note.en: The first group separates nuclear from the noun and from near-looking words; the second separates its atomic sense from its biological and social senses.
note.cn: 第一组把 nuclear 与名词及形近词分开；第二组把它的原子义与生物、社会义分开。

entries.definition: The central body itself; nuclear is the adjective used in nuclear power, nuclear physics or nuclear envelope.
entries.definitionCN: 指中心小体本身；nuclear 是用于 nuclear power、nuclear physics、nuclear envelope 的形容词。

entries.definition: A structure inside the cell nucleus, not the nucleus; it is a noun and never replaces nuclear as a modifier.
entries.definitionCN: 指细胞核内的一个结构，不是细胞核本身；它是名词，不能像 nuclear 那样作修饰语。

entries.definition: Used almost only in nucleic acid; it refers to the chemistry of nuclei, not to nuclear energy.
entries.definitionCN: 几乎只用于 nucleic acid；它指核的化学，而不是核能。

entries.definition: Relating to atoms as wholes; atomic energy can mean energy from the atom generally, while nuclear pins it to the nucleus.
entries.definitionCN: 指与整个原子有关的；atomic energy 可泛指原子能，而 nuclear 明确限定在原子核。

entries.definition: Describing unstable nuclei that emit radiation; a material can be radioactive without being part of a nuclear reactor.
entries.definitionCN: 指不稳定的核发出辐射；某种材料可以具有放射性，却与核反应堆无关。

entries.definition: Located at the middle; it is the everyday word for position and never means atomic or cell nuclei.
entries.definitionCN: 指位于中间，是表示位置的日常词，从不指原子核或细胞核。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: nucleus + -ar: the adjective of the kernel.
normal.cn: nucleus + -ar：果核的形容词。

normal.en: The family runs nucleus, nuclear-powered, nuclear-free and nucleonics.
normal.cn: 同族词有 nucleus、nuclear-powered、nuclear-free、nucleonics。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: nuclear power, nuclear weapon, nuclear family, nuclear envelope.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：核能、核武器、核心家庭、核膜。

normal.en: Context decides whether the nucleus is in an atom or in a cell.
normal.cn: 上下文决定这个核是在原子里还是在细胞里。

normal.en: The nuclear option is a metaphor borrowed from the bomb.
normal.cn: nuclear option 是从核弹借来的比喻。

abstract.en: An atom is a tiny sun with a nucleus at the centre and electrons in orbit.
abstract.cn: 原子像一颗微型太阳，原子核在中心，电子在轨道上。

abstract.en: A nuclear family is a small core with a clear boundary, like a nucleus with its membrane.
abstract.cn: 核心家庭像一个有清晰边界的小核心，如同带膜的细胞核。

abstract.en: The nuclear option is the move that ends the game, like a bomb in a board game.
abstract.cn: 极端手段是终结整局棋的那一步，就像棋盘游戏里的炸弹。

examples.en: Nuclear power produces electricity without burning coal.
examples.cn: 核能发电不燃烧煤炭。

examples.en: The nuclear envelope separates the cell's DNA from the cytoplasm.
examples.cn: 核膜把细胞的 DNA 与细胞质隔开。

examples.en: The country expanded its nuclear medicine programme.
examples.cn: 该国扩大了核医学项目。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「nucleus（核）+ -ar」→ 跟核有关的 → 原子核的、核能的、细胞核的

root: 拉丁语 nux「坚果」→ nucleus「果仁、小核」→ 英语 nucleus；加形容词后缀 -ar 构成 nuclear。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses divide into three families: atomic physics and its power and weapons, cell biology and its envelope, and social or figurative cores such as the nuclear family and the nuclear option.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项分成三族：原子物理及其能量与武器，细胞生物学及其核膜，以及核心家庭、极端手段这类社会或比喻性的核心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tiny centre with electrons or a membrane wrapped around it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个极小的中心，外面绕着一圈电子或一层膜。

branches.en: ATOMIC SCIENCE: the nucleus as an object of study and the discipline built around it.
branches.cn: 原子科学：作为研究对象的原子核，以及围绕它建立的学科。

branches.en: ENERGY AND MEDICINE: power from the nucleus, weapons from the same source, and radioactive tracers.
branches.cn: 能量与医学：来自核的能量，同源的武器，以及放射性示踪剂。

branches.en: CELL BIOLOGY: the nucleus of a living cell and the membrane around it.
branches.cn: 细胞生物学：活细胞的细胞核及其周围的膜。

branches.en: SOCIAL CORE: the small household built around parents and children.
branches.cn: 社会核心：围绕父母与子女建立的小家庭。

branches.en: METAPHOR: the destructive force of the bomb becomes a last-resort political move.
branches.cn: 比喻：核弹的破坏力变成政治上最后才用的手段。

intro.en: Nuclear adds the Latin adjective ending -ar to nucleus; the word then multiplies in compounds.
intro.cn: nuclear 在 nucleus 后加拉丁语形容词词尾 -ar；随后在复合词中大量增殖。

latinIntro.en: Latin nux and nucleus supply the root; -ar comes from Latin -aris. Compounds such as nuclear-powered and nuclear-free are English formations.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nux 与 nucleus 提供词根；-ar 来自拉丁语 -aris。nuclear-powered、nuclear-free 等复合词是英语构造。

items.example: Nuclear reactions change the identity of atoms.
items.exampleCN: 核反应改变原子的身份。

items.example: The nucleus is the cell's control centre.
items.exampleCN: 细胞核是细胞的控制中心。

items.example: A nuclear-powered submarine can stay under for months.
items.exampleCN: 核动力潜艇能在水下停留数月。
该区域被宣布为无核区。
核工程学涵盖反应堆与同位素。
放射性废料需要长期储存。

definition_zh: 立法；立法行为；法律法规（总称）；（某一部）法律
definition_en: the making of laws by an authorized body, or the body of laws so made
core_image: 议事厅里逐条朗读、举手表决，散会后书记员把通过的条文装订成厚册
scene: 辩论持续到深夜，反对党仍要求把每一条都念完再表决。 Parliament passed legislation that rewrites the funding formula.
sceneCN: 这里 legislation 指立法机关通过的法律（第 2 个义项：法规总称）；句意为议会通过了一项改写拨款公式的法律。

pos.zh: 一部法律（可数，常见于美式用法）

forms.label: 复数（指多部法律，多见于美式用法）

derivatives.zh: 立法（legislation 去后缀构成动词，由产物转指制定过程）
立法的（legislate + -ive「有……性质的」，由动作转指属性）
立法者；议员（legislate + -or「行事者」，由动作转指人）
立法机关（legislate + -ure「机构」，由动作转指机关）

senses.title: The making of laws
senses.definition: the process or act of making laws through an authorized body
senses.definitionCN: 由有权机关制定法律的过程或行为
senses.example: Legislation took eighteen months and three committees.
senses.exampleCN: 立法花了十八个月、经过三个委员会。
senses.why: the Latin noun names the bringing of a law, an act rather than a thing.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁名词本指「把法带来」，是行为而非物品。

senses.title: Laws collectively
senses.definition: the whole body of enacted laws on a subject or in a jurisdiction
senses.definitionCN: 某一领域或某一法域已颁行的全部法律
senses.example: Environmental legislation now covers the whole watershed.
senses.exampleCN: 环境法规如今覆盖整个流域。
senses.why: mass-noun use treats statutes as one substance, which is how policy talk usually needs them.
senses.whyCN: 不可数用法把诸多法令当作一种物质，政策讨论通常正需要这样。

senses.title: A single statute
senses.definition: one enacted law, countable especially in American usage
senses.definitionCN: 一部已颁行的法律，在美式用法中可数
senses.example: Two legislations were merged into one act.
senses.exampleCN: 两部法令被合并为一项法案。
senses.why: American usage makes the noun countable because each bill becomes a numbered law.
senses.whyCN: 美式用法把这个名词可数化，因为每项议案都会成为一部编号法律。

senses.title: The legislative process
senses.definition: the staged procedure of reading, amending and voting that a bill must pass
senses.definitionCN: 议案必须经过的宣读、修正与表决的分阶段程序
senses.example: The rules of legislation favour whoever controls the agenda.
senses.exampleCN: 立法程序偏向掌控议程的一方。
senses.why: procedure is the machinery behind the act, and English uses the same noun for both.
senses.whyCN: 程序是行为背后的机器，英语用同一个名词兼指两者。

senses.title: What a legislature enacts
senses.definition: the output of a parliament or congress, as distinct from rules made by agencies
senses.definitionCN: 议会或国会的产出，区别于行政机关自订的规则
senses.example: Primary legislation needs a vote; guidance does not.
senses.exampleCN: 主要立法需要表决，行政指引则不必。
senses.why: the word marks the source of authority, so it separates parliamentary output from administrative rules.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标示权威来源，因此把议会产出与行政规则分开。

senses.title: Delegated legislation
senses.definition: rules made by a minister or agency under powers granted by a statute
senses.definitionCN: 部长或机关依法律授予的权力制定的规则
senses.example: Delegated legislation fills in technical detail the chamber cannot debate.
senses.exampleCN: 次级立法填补议会无法逐条辩论的技术细节。
senses.why: the word travels with the authority to make law, even when that authority has been lent out.
senses.whyCN: 这个词随立法权一同转移，即使该权力是被借出去的。

senses.title: Proposed legislation
senses.definition: a bill or draft still before the chamber, spoken of as future law
senses.definitionCN: 仍在议会审议、被视作未来法律的议案或草案
senses.example: Proposed legislation would cap the fee at ten percent.
senses.exampleCN: 拟议立法将把这个费用上限设为百分之十。
senses.why: the word is applied ahead of enactment because the shape of the law is already visible in the draft.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在通过之前就被使用，因为法律的形状在草案里已经可见。

senses.title: Rules for an organization
senses.titleCN: 引申：组织内部规则体系
senses.definition: the formal rules by which a body governs its own members or processes
senses.definitionCN: 某机构管理自身成员或流程的成文规则
senses.example: The society's legislation on conflicts of interest is three pages long.
senses.exampleCN: 该学会关于利益冲突的规则有三页纸。
senses.why: private bodies borrow the word when their rules begin to function like statutes.
senses.whyCN: 私人机构在其规则开始像法令一样运作时，便借用了这个词。

intro.en: Legislation comes from Latin legis latio 'a bringing of a law', from lex 'law' and latio 'a bringing', the noun of latus, the past participle of ferre 'to carry'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: legislation 来自拉丁 legis latio「把法带来」，由 lex「法」与 latio「带来」构成，后者是 ferre「搬运」的过去分词 latus 的名词形式。年代均为约数。

items.en: Lex meant 'law, statute, a motion put to the people'. Its deeper origin is not established; the old link to legere 'to read' is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: lex 意为「法、法令、提交民众的动议」。其更深来源未得到证明；与 legere「读」的旧联系只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Ferre 'to carry, bring' has the suppletive participle latus, from which latio 'a bringing' is formed; the two verbs were already fused in classical usage.
items.cn: ferre「搬运、带来」的过去分词为异干互补的 latus，由其构成 latio「带来」；两者在古典用法中已合并。

items.en: The phrase legis latio named the bringing of a bill before the assembly, a procedural act rather than the text itself.
items.cn: legis latio 这一说法指把议案带到大会之前的程序性行为，而非文本本身。

items.en: Medieval Latin legislatio generalized the phrase into the making of laws by any authorized body.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁 legislatio 把这一说法一般化，指任何有权机关制定法律。

items.en: French législation passed into English in the seventeenth century, first as the act and soon after as the body of laws.
items.cn: 法语 législation 在 17 世纪进入英语，先指立法行为，不久也指法律总体。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the earliest English citation is not precisely dated, and the origin of lex itself remains unsettled, so any older form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：最早的英语书证没有确切年代；lex 本身的来源仍无定论，为其提出的更早形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one shares the lex or legisl- stem; group two holds words for laws and for the making of them.
note.cn: 第一组共享 lex 或 legisl- 词干；第二组是关于法律与制定法律的词。

entries.definition: Describing a body or power that makes law; it cannot stand for the laws themselves.
entries.definitionCN: 描述制定法律的机关或权力；不能指法律本身。

entries.definition: The assembly that makes law, formed with -ure 'place or body'; a different thing from the laws it makes.
entries.definitionCN: 制定法律的议会，由 -ure「场所、机构」构成；与其所制定的法律是两回事。

entries.definition: One member who makes law; the noun names a role, not an output.
entries.definitionCN: 制定法律的成员之一；指角色，而非产出。

entries.definition: From Latin legitimus 'lawful', built on lex but through a different adjective; it means lawful, not law-making.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 legitimus「合法的」，虽出 lex 却经另一形容词；意为合法，而非立法。

entries.definition: A single rule or the whole body of rules; legislation is the making of it or the output as a mass.
entries.definitionCN: 单条规则或全部规则；legislation 指制定过程或作为总体的产出。

entries.definition: A single law passed by a legislature, countable and technical; legislation is the wider mass noun.
entries.definitionCN: 立法机关通过的单项法律，可数且技术化；legislation 是更宽的总称。

entries.definition: Detailed rules issued by an agency under a statute, usually not requiring a parliamentary vote.
entries.definitionCN: 机关依法令发布的细则，通常不经议会表决。

entries.definition: A draft law still under consideration; legislation names what it becomes, or the process of making it.
entries.definitionCN: 仍在审议的草案；legislation 指它最终成为的东西，或制定它的过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: legis latio: the bringing of a law, so the word began as a motion carried forward.
normal.cn: legis latio：把法带来，因此这个词本是一项被送上前的动议。

normal.en: The family runs legislate, legislation, legislative, legislator, legislature.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 legislate、legislation、legislative、legislator、legislature。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split act from output: pass legislation, delegated legislation, environmental legislation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配分出行为与产出：通过立法、授权立法、环境立法。

normal.en: Contrast the pair: a bill is the draft, legislation is the making and the mass of laws.
normal.cn: 对照这一对：bill 是草案，legislation 是制定过程与法律总体。

normal.en: Watch the false friend legitimate: lawful, but built on a different adjective of lex.
normal.cn: 提防假朋友 legitimate：意为合法，却由 lex 的另一形容词构成。

abstract.en: Picture a text carried by hand across a hall before anyone votes on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一份文本在被人手捧着穿过大厅，之后才有人表决。

abstract.en: Picture shelves that grow a new thick volume every session.
abstract.cn: 想象书架每开一次会就多一本厚册。

abstract.en: Picture a rule that must be read aloud before it can bind anyone.
abstract.cn: 想象一条规则必须先被大声读出，才能约束任何人。

examples.en: The state's legislation on groundwater is older than its mapping.
examples.cn: 该州关于地下水的立法比水文测绘还要早。

examples.en: Delegated legislation filled in the standards the chamber left blank.
examples.cn: 次级立法填上了议会留白的技术标准。

examples.en: Industry lobbied against the proposed legislation for two years.
examples.cn: 业界游说反对这项拟议立法达两年。

dict_mnemonic.text: legis（法）+ lation（带来）＝ 把法带到台面上；记「念一遍、改一遍、举一次手」。

root: 拉丁 legis latio「把法带来」= lex「法」（更深来源不确定，与 legere「读」的联系仅为假说）+ latio「带来」（来自 ferre「搬运」的过去分词 latus）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow a bill from act to archive: making law, the mass of law, one statute, the procedure, parliamentary output, delegated rules, drafts not yet passed, and the rules of a private body.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项随一项议案从行为走到档案：立法、法律总体、单部法律、程序、议会产出、授权规则、尚未通过的草案，以及私人机构的规则。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a text read aloud, amended, voted on, then bound into a thick volume.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份文本被朗读、修正、表决，最后装订进厚册。

branches.en: ACT AND MASS: the making of law, then the whole body it accumulates into.
branches.cn: 行为与总体：先制定，再累积成整体。

branches.en: ONE VOLUME: the countable unit inside the mass.
branches.cn: 单册：总体之中的可数单位。

branches.en: THE MACHINE: procedure at work, and the authority that makes its output law.
branches.cn: 机器：程序在运转，以及使其产成为法律的权威。

branches.en: LENT POWER: rule-making handed to ministers and agencies.
branches.cn: 借出的权力：规则制定权交到部长与机关手里。

branches.en: BEFORE AND AFTER THE HALL: drafts spoken of as law, and private bodies drafting their own.
branches.cn: 大厅前后：草案已被当作法律谈论，私人机构也自订规则。

intro.en: Legislation joins a Latin noun for law to a Latin noun for bringing, and the second element still appears in English words of transfer.
intro.cn: legislation 把拉丁语「法」的名词与「带来」的名词接在一起，后一成分仍出现在英语的转移类词中。

latinIntro.en: Lex supplies legal, legitimate and legislate; latus and ferre supply transfer, refer and relate.
latinIntro.cn: lex 衍生 legal、legitimate、legislate；latus 与 ferre 衍生 transfer、refer、relate。

items.example: Lex is the root of legal and legislate.
items.exampleCN: lex 是 legal 与 legislate 的词根。

items.example: Its participle latus hides inside latio.
items.exampleCN: 其分词 latus 藏在 latio 里。

items.example: Legis latio is the bringing of a bill.
items.exampleCN: legis latio 就是把议案带来。

items.example: The chamber legislates twice a year.
Legislation followed the report by a year.
items.exampleCN: 报告之后一年才有了立法。

items.example: The legislator read the amendment aloud.
items.exampleCN: 立法者大声读了修正案。

items.example: A legitimate claim differs from a popular one.
items.exampleCN: 合法的诉求与受欢迎的诉求不同。

definition_zh: 在……旁边；与……并排；与……一起、与……合作；靠（码头、船舷）边；并存
definition_en: at the side of something, together with someone, or close to the side of a ship or pier
core_image: 两条船的船舷贴得很近，几乎碰在一起
scene: 天还没亮，补给船贴着石砌的岸壁缓缓靠过去。 The supply boat came alongside the pier just before dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 alongside 是「靠在……边」（第 3 个义项：船或码头旁的贴近位置）；句意为补给船在黎明前靠上了码头。画面里可辨认的是缆绳、石壁与船头的水痕。

pos.zh: 介词：在……旁边；与……一起；靠（船、码头）边

derivatives.zh: 由 alongside 加 of 构成的完整形式，美式英语中表示「在……旁边」
由同一 along- 成分加 shore 构成的相关词，义为「沿岸的；沿着海岸」
与 along 同源的旧形式，义为「沿着」，与 alongside 共用 along- 成分

senses.title: Next to the side of something
senses.definition: at or by the side of something, with the two running side by side
senses.definitionCN: 在某物的侧边，两者并行排列
senses.example: A row of poplars grows alongside the railway.
senses.exampleCN: 一排白杨沿着铁路生长。
senses.why: The word joins along and side: the whole length of one thing is laid next to the side of another, so the two edges run parallel.
senses.whyCN: alongside 由 along 与 side 复合：把一样东西的整条长度贴到另一样东西的侧边上，两条边于是并行，这就是「在……旁边」。

senses.title: Working together as a partner
senses.definition: working or acting together with someone, especially as a partner or helper
senses.definitionCN: 与他人一起工作或行动，尤指作为伙伴或帮手
senses.example: Nurses worked alongside the doctors through the whole night.
senses.exampleCN: 护士们整夜与医生并肩工作。
senses.why: Two people who walk the same length on the same side are partners; the physical side-by-side becomes cooperation without any change of words.
senses.whyCN: 两个人贴着同一侧、走同一段路，就是并肩；空间上的「并排」不加一字就引申为工作上的「一起、协作」。

senses.title: Close to the side of a ship or pier
senses.definition: in nautical use, close to the side of a ship, a pier or a wharf
senses.definitionCN: 航海用语，指贴近船、码头或突堤的侧边
senses.example: The supply boat came alongside the pier just before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 补给船在黎明前靠上了码头。
senses.why: This is the compound's first home: sailors needed a word for a boat lying against another boat's side, and the ordinary side of a ship supplied it.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个复合词最早的落脚处：水手需要形容一条船贴住另一条船的侧边，而船本来就有一个「侧边」，于是这个词先用在码头与船舷上。

senses.title: Adverb: drawing near the side
senses.definition: used as an adverb, close to the side of something, especially of a ship drawing near
senses.definitionCN: 作副词时表示靠近某物的侧边，尤指船靠过来
senses.example: The pilot boat drew alongside and a ladder was lowered.
senses.exampleCN: 引航船靠了过来，一条梯子被放了下去。
senses.why: Drop the object and the word turns into an adverb: the side is still there, but the sentence no longer names what is being approached.
senses.whyCN: 省略宾语后，它就成了副词：侧边仍在，只是句子不再点明贴近的是哪样东西，于是表示「靠过来、在旁边」。

senses.title: Alongside of: the fuller form
senses.definition: in American usage, the fuller form alongside of, used before a noun with the same meaning
senses.definitionCN: 美式用法中更完整的形式 alongside of，接名词时意思相同
senses.example: A small shed stood alongside of the barn.
senses.exampleCN: 谷仓旁边立着一间小棚屋。
senses.why: English often pairs a preposition with of to make a relation explicit; of adds nothing new but makes the side relation feel complete.
senses.whyCN: 英语常给介词再配一个 of，把关系说死；of 不添新义，只是让「在旁边」这层关系显得完整，于是有了 alongside of。

senses.title: Existing side by side
senses.definition: existing or happening at the same time as something else, without replacing it
senses.definitionCN: 与另一事物同时存在或发生，并不取代它
senses.example: Traditional remedies are still used alongside modern drugs in the clinic.
senses.exampleCN: 在这家诊所里，传统疗法与现代药物仍并存使用。
senses.why: If two things run on the same length without pushing each other away, they can coexist; side by side in space becomes side by side in time.
senses.whyCN: 两样东西在同一段上并行、谁也不挤走谁，就可以共存；空间上的并排因此转成时间上的「并存」。

intro.en: Alongside is a transparent English compound of along and side, and it began as a sailor's word.
intro.cn: alongside 是 along 与 side 组成的透明复合词，最初是水手的用语。

items.en: The first element is andlang, the whole length of, built from and- plus lang long.
items.cn: 第一部分是 andlang「整条长度」，由 and- 加 lang「长」构成。

items.en: Side meant flank or the long edge of a thing, and it is the second element of the compound.
items.cn: side 意为「侧面、长边」，是这个复合词的第二部分。

items.en: The compound is recorded in nautical writing in the eighteenth century, meaning close to the side of a ship; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个复合词一般认为自十八世纪起见于航海文字，意为「贴近船舷」；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The meaning widened from ships to anything with a side, such as roads, rivers and buildings.
items.cn: 词义从船只扩展到一切有侧边的东西，如道路、河流与建筑。

items.en: The figurative sense together with, and the fuller American form alongside of, become common in ordinary prose.
items.cn: 引申义「与……一起」以及美式完整形式 alongside of 在普通书面语中变得常见。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the two elements of the compound, the shore compound built on the same first element, and the old form in -st; the near-meaning group holds words for side, equality and addition.
note.cn: 形近组收复合词的两个成分、用同一前项构成的沿岸词，以及带 -st 的旧形式；近义组收表示侧旁、并列与附加的词。

entries.definition: The first element of the compound, meaning from one end towards the other.
entries.definitionCN: 复合词的第一部分，义为「沿着、从一端到另一端」。

entries.definition: The second element, meaning the flank or long edge of something.
entries.definitionCN: 复合词的第二部分，义为某物的侧面或长边。

entries.definition: An adjective and adverb meaning along the shore, built on the same along- element.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词与副词，义为「沿岸的、沿着海岸」，由同一个 along- 成分构成。

entries.definition: An old form meaning along, now found only in older texts.
entries.definitionCN: 旧形式，义同 along「沿着」，今只见于较早的文本。

entries.definition: At the side of something; like alongside, but without the idea of running the whole length.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……旁边」；与 alongside 相近，但不含「沿着整段」的意思。

entries.definition: Side by side and facing the same way; the closest match for the parallel sense.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「并排地、并肩地」，与 alongside 的「并排」义最接近。

entries.definition: In addition to; it looks like beside but has moved into the sense of addition, as along with can.
entries.definitionCN: 介词与副词，义为「除……之外、此外」；形似 beside，却和 along with 一样转向了「附加」义。

entries.definition: Running in the same direction at a constant distance; the geometric picture behind side by side.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词与名词，义为「平行的、平行线」，正是「并排」背后的几何画面。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two visible elements along and side, the nautical origin, and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用看得见的两个成分 along 与 side、它的航海来源，以及这个词常出现的短语。

normal.en: Along plus side: a whole length laid against a side.
normal.cn: along 加 side：把一整条长度贴到一个侧边上。

normal.en: The word began with boats, because a ship's side is the most literal side there is.
normal.cn: 这个词从船开始，因为船舷是最字面意义上的「侧边」。

normal.en: Work alongside keeps the same picture, with people standing where boats once stood.
normal.cn: work alongside 保留同一个画面，只是把船换成了人。

normal.en: Alongside of only adds of, so the side relation is spelled out.
normal.cn: alongside of 只是多加一个 of，把「在旁边」的关系说白。

normal.en: Two old customs surviving alongside each other are simply two things on one line.
normal.cn: 两种并存的老习俗，不过是同一条线上的两样东西。

abstract.en: Two hulls float so close that the paint on both sides almost touches.
abstract.cn: 两条船身贴得极近，两侧的漆几乎碰到一起。

abstract.en: Two runners keep the same stride on two parallel tracks for the whole race.
abstract.cn: 两名跑者在两条平行跑道上，整场保持同样的步幅。

abstract.en: Take the boat away and the two sides remain, still parallel, still level.
abstract.cn: 把船移走，两条边还在，仍然平行，仍然齐平。

examples.en: A row of poplars grows alongside the railway.
examples.cn: 一排白杨沿着铁路生长。

examples.en: Nurses worked alongside the doctors through the whole night.
examples.cn: 护士们整夜与医生并肩工作。

examples.en: Old fishing customs survive alongside modern tourism in the village.
examples.cn: 在这个村子里，古老的捕鱼习俗与现代旅游业并存。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿朗赛德」——两条船把船舷贴在一起：在……旁边；与……一起。

root: 由 along 与 side 复合而成：along 来自古英语 andlang「整条长度」，side 意为「侧面、长边」。十八世纪起在航海文字中表示「贴近船舷」，十九世纪扩展到道路、河流、建筑等一切有侧边之物，再由「并排」引申出「与……一起」「并存」。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses keep one geometry: a length laid against a side. The side can belong to a road, a partner, a pier, or another custom that simply coexists.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项保持同一个几何关系：把一条长度贴到一个侧边上。这个侧边可以属于道路、伙伴、码头，也可以属于另一种只是并存着的习俗。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two edges run parallel, so close that they almost touch.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条边并行延伸，近得几乎相触。

branches.en: THE SIDE: one length is laid beside another, and the two run parallel.
branches.cn: 侧边线：一条长度被贴到另一条旁边，两者并行。

branches.en: THE COMPANY: standing side by side becomes working together, and then merely existing at the same time.
branches.cn: 共处线：并排而立变成一起工作，再退一步就是同时存在。

branches.en: THE HARBOUR: the compound's oldest home is a boat lying against a ship or a pier.
branches.cn: 港湾线：这个复合词最早的家，是一条船贴住另一条船或码头。

branches.en: THE ADVERB: with the object left out, the word simply says that something is close to the side.

definition_zh: 经济学；经济状况；经济因素；成本效益
definition_en: the academic study of how goods, money and services are produced and used, or the financial facts and costs of a particular situation
core_image: 黑板上画着供求两条曲线，交点被红笔圈住
scene: 黑板上画着供求两条曲线，交点被红笔圈住。 Economics explains why prices rise when supply falls.
sceneCN: 这里 economics 是「经济学」（第 1 个义项：研究生产、贸易与货币的学科）；句意为经济学解释了供给下降时价格为何上涨。图中可辨识物件：黑板、两条曲线、红笔圈。

pos.zh: 名词：经济学；经济状况；经济因素；成本效益

senses.title: The academic study of the economy
senses.titleCN: 经济学：研究经济活动的学科
senses.definition: the social science that studies how goods, services and money are produced, distributed and consumed
senses.definitionCN: 研究商品、服务与货币如何被生产、分配和消费的社会科学
senses.example: Economics explains why prices rise when supply falls.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学解释了供给下降时价格为何上涨。
senses.why: The Greek root named household management, and -ics marks a field of study, so economics is the discipline built around that management.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根意为「管理家户」，-ics 标记一门学科，因此 economics 就是围绕这种管理建立起来的学问。

senses.title: The economic state of a place
senses.titleCN: 经济状况：某地的经济情况
senses.definition: the financial condition and performance of a country, region or industry
senses.definitionCN: 国家、地区或行业在财政上的状况与表现
senses.example: The report describes the economics of the fishing towns on the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告描述了沿海渔镇的经济状况。
senses.why: The discipline name shifted onto its own subject matter: what the subject studies can also be called its economics.
senses.whyCN: 学科名称移到了它所研究的对象上：这门学问研究的东西，也可以被称为它的 economics。

senses.title: The cost-and-benefit calculation
senses.titleCN: 经济账：某项计划或交易的成本效益
senses.definition: the practical calculation of costs and returns in a particular plan, deal or activity
senses.definitionCN: 对某项计划、交易或活动的成本与回报所作的实际核算
senses.example: The economics of the deal collapsed when fuel prices doubled.
senses.exampleCN: 燃料价格翻倍后，这笔交易的经济账就算不过来了。
senses.why: A household manager weighs cost against return, and this everyday calculation is the practical echo of the academic subject.
senses.whyCN: 当家人要权衡成本与回报，这种日常核算就是这门学科在实务中的回声。

intro.en: Economics is a learned Greek compound whose English name for the discipline dates only from the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: economics 是学术性的希腊语复合词，它作为学科名称在英语中出现仅始于十九世纪。

items.en: Oikos meant house or household, the unit within which resources were managed.
items.cn: oikos 意为房子、家户，是资源被管理的单位。

items.en: Nomos meant law, rule or custom, giving oikonomia the sense of household rule.
items.cn: nomos 意为法律、规则或习俗，使 oikonomia 带上「家户规则」的意思。

items.en: Oikonomia covered household management and later public finance.
items.cn: oikonomia 涵盖家务管理，后来也指公共财政。

items.en: Latin carried the word into European learning, where it still meant management rather than a market system.
items.cn: 拉丁语把这个词带入欧洲学术，当时它仍指管理，而不是市场体系。

items.en: Political economy was shortened to economics as a name for the new university discipline; the exact first use is uncertain.
items.cn: 随着新的大学学科成形，political economy 被缩为 economics；确切首次使用年代不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the four words most often confused in this family; the near-meaning group gathers names for financial study and practice.
note.cn: 形近组收这一词族中最常被混淆的四个词；近义组收表示金融研究与实务的名称。

entries.definition: The real system of production and trade, not the study of it.
entries.definitionCN: 真实的生产与贸易体系，而不是对它的研究。

entries.definition: An adjective for the economy or for economics.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指经济或经济学的。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning thrifty or cheap to run.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「节约的、使用成本低的」。

entries.definition: The study and management of money, especially at public or corporate level.
entries.definitionCN: 对金钱的研究与管理，尤指公共或公司层面。

entries.definition: The recording and checking of financial accounts.
entries.definitionCN: 对财务账目进行记录与核对。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the discipline, its subject matter and its practical calculation in three separate boxes.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把「学科」「研究对象」与「实际核算」分放在三个盒子里。

normal.en: Economics with -ics is the classroom; economy without it is the world outside.
normal.cn: 带 -ics 的 economics 是课堂；去掉它的 economy 是课堂外的世界。

normal.en: The same word can mean the subject, the condition it studies, or the sum done on a deal.
normal.cn: 同一个词可以指学科、它所研究的状况，或一笔交易上的算式。

normal.en: Oikos plus nomos: a house plus a rule, scaled up to a nation.
normal.cn: oikos 加 nomos：一所房子加一条规则，再放大到一个国家。

normal.en: The economics of a deal is a small household sum written large.
normal.cn: 一笔交易的 economics，就是放大写出的家常账。

normal.en: An economist is the person, economics is the field: one suffix marks the other's practitioner.
normal.cn: economist 是人，economics 是领域：一个后缀标出另一个的从业者。

abstract.en: Picture two curves crossing on a blackboard, with a red circle around the crossing.
abstract.cn: 想象黑板上两条曲线相交，交点被红圈圈住。

abstract.en: The same crossing can stand for a theory, a country's condition, or a deal that no longer pays.
abstract.cn: 同一个交点可以代表一套理论、一个国家的状况，或一笔不再划算的交易。

abstract.en: Economics means the rules of the house, studied and applied.
abstract.cn: economics 意味着「家户的规则」，既被研究，也被应用。

examples.en: Economics explains why prices rise when supply falls.
examples.cn: 经济学解释了供给下降时价格为何上涨。

examples.en: The report describes the economics of the fishing towns on the coast.
examples.cn: 这份报告描述了沿海渔镇的经济状况。

examples.en: The economics of the deal collapsed when fuel prices doubled.
examples.cn: 燃料价格翻倍后，这笔交易的经济账就算不过来了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「伊科诺米克斯」——黑板两条曲线，红笔一圈

root: 希腊语 oikonomia「家务管理」由 oikos「家户」与 nomos「规则」构成，经拉丁语 oeconomia 进入欧洲学术；十九世纪以 -ics 定名经济学。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of economics: the university subject, the economic condition it studies, and the cost-benefit sum done in practice.
sensesIntro.cn: economics 的三个义项：大学学科、它所研究的经济状况，以及实务中算出的成本效益。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two curves cross on a blackboard and the crossing is circled in red.
core.cn: 核心意象：黑板上两条曲线相交，交点被红圈圈住。

branches.en: THE DISCIPLINE: the university subject and its methods.
branches.cn: 学科线：大学里的学科及其方法。

branches.en: THE CONDITION: the real financial state of a place or industry.
branches.cn: 状况线：一个地方或行业真实的财政状态。

branches.en: THE SUM: costs and returns calculated for one plan.
branches.cn: 算式线：针对一项计划算出的成本与回报。

branches.en: THE SUBJECT MATTER: the discipline and what it studies share one name.
